raw.title: Community Lead
raw.description:
Accurx is solving healthcare productivity for the NHS

At Accurx, we’ve supported thousands of healthcare organisations to deliver care for over 60 million patients. We’re used by 98% of GP practices and in 68% of NHS Trusts - that’s over 200,000 NHS staff each week.

For decades, the NHS has struggled with fragmented systems that slow everything down and leave patients waiting. We're changing that. We’re transforming how NHS staff triage and prioritise patient demand, cut the admin that eats into clinical time, and work as one team across the system.

We've spent eight years proving care doesn't always need to happen in an appointment. In the best triage practices today, 40% of patient demand is resolved without one. Now we're taking that model system-wide – using AI to automate the work that slows healthcare down, connecting every part of the NHS and building the platform on which the future of healthcare work gets done.

About the role

You’ll support and scale one of the most engaged clinical communities in the UK. Our users already talk to each other every day. They share what works, solve problems together and advocate for better ways of working. But those conversations are spread across WhatsApp groups and Facebook channels, with no platform or structure behind them. Our ambassador programme is also ready to be taken further.

As our Community Lead reporting to the Head of Marketing, you’ll shape how healthcare professionals connect, learn from one another and drive change across the NHS. You’ll turn organic momentum into a scalable community that measurably drives product adoption, peer-to-peer learning and brand trust.

The challenges you’ll take on

  • Building strategic and large-scale communities: Shaping and delivering the long-term vision for our primary and secondary care communities, with community playing a clear role in driving product adoption and brand advocacy, not just engagement. You'll be actively running community initiatives, as well as setting the strategic direction.

  • Turning unstructured clinical conversations into scalable content: Creating repeatable ways to transform high-volume community conversations into user-led content, learning assets and programmes, using strong storytelling to make Accurx's value clear and compelling across the market.

  • Scaling advocacy through ambassadors and peer influence: Owning and evolving our ambassador programme that enable clinicians to influence their peers authentically, and aligning it closely with product and marketing priorities.

  • Owning our community platform and programmes: Choosing and implementing the right long-term platform to bring our community together, and deciding when existing tools are “good enough”. You’ll help Accurx invest in the right processes and operating models for a growing, multi-product, multi-care-setting community.

You should apply if...

  • You have proven experience building and growing communities in the thousands, ideally in SaaS, tech or healthcare. This is essential for the role.

  • You've used community as a core driver of commercial growth, product adoption or brand advocacy, rather than it being primarily focused on support, account management or research.

  • You have a strong track record of designing, running or scaling ambassador programmes and super-user initiatives that drive peer-to-peer learning and influence.

  • You can point to clear examples of turning unstructured community conversations into scalable, user-led content, with strong written communication and storytelling skills.

  • You bring a data-informed and tool-savvy mindset, using signals, feedback and AI to scale insight capture and content without losing authenticity.

  • You're a strong cross-functional collaborator, comfortable partnering closely with Product, User Research, Implementation, Product Marketing and Events.

What's in it for you?

You'll be joining an established but fast-growing Tech for Good movement, where we're led by our Principles and our mission to Solve Healthcare Productivity.

  • £65,000 - £85,000 salary + £30,000 share options

  • Benefits to suit you: adjust your healthcare cover, your pension or life insurance, whatever stage you're at in life

  • Flexible Working: We are an office first culture and ask that you're in our (dog-friendly) Shoreditch office 3 days a week, with core hours of 10am–4pm

  • Time off: You'll get 28 days of holiday (plus bank holidays) and up to 4 weeks to work from anywhere per year

  • Family matters: We offer enhanced parental leave, fertility support and parental loss support

  • We have our very own Chef! Free healthy breakfasts, snacks and lunches will be provided, with the occasional sweet treat!

Want to know more about the company or the hiring process? Check out our Careers page and Candidate hub. Find us across social media: LinkedIn, and YouTube.

Compensation: £65K – £85K • £30K Equity

  • • £65K – £85K • £30K Equity

About the Role

We hire builders with founder-level energy—people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do.

As Director, Regulatory Compliance (UK), you will serve as the senior compliance authority and strategic partner for Airwallex’s rapidly expanding UK presence. Operating as a licensed Electronic Money Institution (EMI) supervised by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), Airwallex requires compliance leadership that sees regulatory integrity not as a roadblock, but as a critical commercial enabler and competitive differentiator.

In this role, you will lead our UK compliance framework, serve as the primary interface with local regulators and industry bodies, and work cross-functionally across Product, Strategy, Commercial, and Operations to safely launch cutting-edge payment infrastructure.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead UK Regulatory Compliance: Lead a UK-based team of regulatory compliance professionals; own and continuously evolve the UK compliance management system, policies, registers, and operational controls to ensure ongoing compliance with FCA handbooks, PSRs, EMRs, and UK AML/CTF regimes.

  • Drive FCA Engagement: Act as the principal point of contact for the FCA, handling regulatory inquiries, notifications, audits, thematic reviews, and routine reporting with transparency and authority.

  • Product & Commercial Advisory: Partner early with Product, Commercial, and International Expansion teams to design compliant-by-default cross-border payment, issuing, acquiring, and embedded finance architectures.

  • Safeguarding & Governance: Oversee compliance aspects of key UK regulatory regimes including safeguardingand Consumer Duty in close partnership with Finance, Risk, Product, and other teams.

  • Regulatory Horizon Scanning: Monitor domestic and international regulatory developments (e.g., Consumer Duty, operational resilience, PSR APP fraud reimbursement schemes) and proactively translate emerging rules into pragmatic technical and operational roadmaps.

  • Team Leadership & Culture: Build, coach, and scale a high-caliber UK compliance advisory and operations team while fostering a company-wide culture of risk accountability and ethical rigor.

  • Board & Committee Reporting: Prepare and deliver clear, actionable regulatory compliance reporting and key risk indicator (KRI) updates to executive leadership, local operating boards, and audit/risk committees.

What We’re Looking For

Essentials

  • 10+ years of regulatory compliance experience within UK fintech, payment services (EMIs/APIs), neo-banking, or modern global financial institutions.

  • Leadership Track Record: At least 4+ years managing and developing high-performing compliance teams in high-growth environments.

  • Deep Regulatory Knowledge: Expert grasp of UK financial regulations, including the Payment Services Regulations (PSRs), Electronic Money Regulations (EMRs), FCA Principles for Businesses, and Consumer Duty standards.

  • FCA Interface Experience: Direct track record of managing formal regulator relationships, supervisory inspections, or key authorization filings with the FCA.

  • Pragmatic Problem-Solving: Ability to interpret complex regulatory requirements through a first-principles lens, providing creative, commercial, and defensible paths forward.

  • Executive Presence: Strong communication, negotiation, and written advocacy skills capable of influencing board members, executive partners, and external regulatory bodies.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Prior experience holding an approved person / Senior Management Function (SMF) role under the FCA regime.

  • Background handling regulatory aspects of cross-border multi-currency schemes, merchant acquiring, or credit/lending adjacencies.

  • Relevant legal qualification or industry certifications (e.g., ICA Diploma in Governance, Risk & Compliance).

You’ll Thrive Here If

  • You own the outcome: You don't wait for permission to solve structural bottlenecks—give you a complex regulatory challenge, and you chart the solution.

  • You’re commercially astute: You understand that compliance is an enabler of sustainable hyper-growth, not an isolated checklist.

  • You balance technical precision with plain-English clarity: You can dissect statutory instruments line by line, then distill the essence clearly for engineers, sales leads, and executives.

  • You’re not precious about traditional playbooks: You push hard from first principles, challenging legacy banking compliance norms with modernized, technology-driven solutions.

  • You value in-person collaboration: You thrive working shoulder-to-shoulder with cross-functional leaders in our London hub.

What Success Looks Like

  • Within 3 Months: Complete a comprehensive assessment of our existing UK compliance controls, policies, and FCA commitments; build alignment with key UK commercial leads and partner banks.

  • Within 6 Months: Streamline product approval compliance workflows; enhance local risk governance reporting; and lead strategic readiness for any pending UK regulatory changes.

  • Within 12 Months: Institutionalize a top-tier UK compliance function that scales seamlessly with transaction volume and new market offerings while maintaining an immaculate standing with the FCA.

Why Join Airwallex

  • Competitive base salary, performance incentives, and meaningful equity.

  • Dynamic, global culture with clear paths for rapid professional development.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full.

 

About the Team

The Financial Crime Compliance (FCC) team at Airwallex is a strategically vital function operating under a clear Three Lines of Defense model. As the independent second line, FCC owns the global AML/CTF program, sanctions framework, risk assessment methodology, and governance infrastructure across all global entities. As Airwallex scales into new markets and deepens its engagement with global regulatory bodies, we are building a world-class compliance organization capable of managing complex financial crime risks at scale. This is an environment where you will tackle high-impact challenges, shape global fintech risk strategies, and help establish foundations for long-term growth.

What you'll do

As Senior Director, AML & Sanctions, Governance & Policy, you will shape and scale Airwallex’s global financial crime policy and risk based program, establish risk appetite and design global risk assessment processes, and define governance frameworks, ensuring compliance is a strategic enabler of growth. You will establish the baseline core compliance standards while guiding regional adaptations, oversee definition of controls across the FCC control framework, strengthen executive risk reporting, oversee risk-informed product engineering, and defend the integrity of the platform before global regulators and institutional partners. You will work closely with the Chief Regulatory and Compliance Officer, Global Head of FCC and senior leaders across the business to turn complex compliance trends into clear action, and shape strategic priorities and initiatives while scaling a high-performing, multi-disciplinary global team.

This role is based in London.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the evolution and maintenance of Airwallex's Global Core FCC Policy Framework, ensuring the compliance baseline meets the expectations of global regulators while supporting business growth and regional scalability.

  • Lead the definition and oversight of the FCC governance model and risk management framework, including establishment of risk appetite incorporating business strategy, establishing the risk management framework, including risk acceptance & governance structure, and overseeing design and execution of the enterprise risk assessment

  • Define the methodology, thresholds, and data-scoring models used to identify and mitigate financial crime risks globally, partnering with Product, Data Science, and Engineering executives to embed automated compliance controls into the proprietary platform.

  • Translate complex compliance data, issues, and audit findings into clear, decision-useful reporting for executive leadership and the Board’s Audit and Risk Committee, establishing clear protocols for material risk escalations.

  • Oversee the strategy for regulatory examination defense and disclosure governance, ensuring the team delivers uniform, legally defensible evidence portfolios to global regulators and external clearing partners.

  • Drive a unified, risk-aware compliance culture across the organization by establishing the strategic vision for global financial crime training and capability building from engineering to sales teams.

  • Support the Global Head of FCC and Chief Regulatory and Compliance Officer in setting and overseeing strategic FCC program priorities and continuous improvement initiatives

  • Build and lead a high-performing global second line team of compliance attorneys, quantitative risk modelers, policy writers, and governance managers, supporting Airwallex’s growth with technology-enabled compliance oversight.

 
 

Who you are

We're looking for people who meet the minimum requirements for this role. The preferred qualifications are great to have, but are not mandatory.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Law, Criminology, Public Policy, Finance, Business Administration, International Relations, or a related analytical field.

  • CAMS certification or an equivalent globally recognized compliance credential (e.g., ICA International Diploma in AML).

  • 12 to 15+ years of experience in AML, Sanctions, and Financial Crime Compliance within financial services, fintech, payments, or banking.

  • At least 5+ years leading a global or multi-jurisdictional compliance policy, governance, or risk methodology function at a senior level.

  • Proven experience designing enterprise-wide risk assessment frameworks and maintaining highly centralized global policies with localized regional addenda.

  • Demonstrated experience preparing risk papers and leading the defense during high-stakes regulatory examinations and internal or external audits.

  • A high-ownership, pragmatic approach, with excellent written communication and stakeholder management skills to influence cross-functional executives and board audiences.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Advanced degree such as a Juris Doctor (JD), Master of Laws (LLM), or a Master’s degree in Regulatory Compliance or Financial Crime.

  • Advanced professional designations such as CAMS-Audit, CGSS (Certified Global Sanctions Specialist), or CAMS-RM (Risk Management).

  • Deep fintech and payments experience, including a strong understanding of cross-border payment mechanisms, virtual accounts, multi-currency wallets, or multi-entity regulated groups.

  • Experience partnering directly with Product, Data Science, and Engineering teams to hardcode policy thresholds into automated transaction monitoring, screening, and onboarding workflows.

  • Strong data literacy and a clear bias toward digital modernization, including the use of automated GRC systems, dashboards, and technology-enabled tools to improve compliance office efficiency.

The Enterprise Business team partners with some of the most sophisticated and high-potential businesses in the world, helping them leverage Airwallex’s products to scale globally. We work closely with product, engineering, marketing and operations teams to solve complex problems for our customers and deliver long-term value. You’ll join a collaborative, ambitious and supportive team that thrives on ownership, customer impact and continuous improvement.

What you'll do

As a Technical Account Manager, you’ll be the trusted technical advisor for a portfolio of enterprise and high‑growth customers across Europe. You’ll sit at the intersection of product, engineering and commercial teams: guiding complex API integrations, troubleshooting issues, and using data to drive adoption, expansion and long‑term retention. You’ll combine deep technical understanding of APIs and payment flows with strong stakeholder management skills – from hands‑on engineers through to senior commercial leaders.

This role is based in London, with a 3 days in office policy.

Responsibilities:

  • Act as the technical owner for a portfolio of customers integrating and scaling on Airwallex’s platforms (APIs, SDKs and system integrations), with a solid understanding of complex technical architectures.

  • Build deep, hands‑on expertise in Airwallex’s payment, treasury, issuing and embedded finance products, advising customers on best‑practice integration patterns and optimisation opportunities.

  • Diagnose and resolve complex technical and operational challenges across the stack, coordinating with Commercial, Engineering, Product and Compliance teams to drive timely, high‑quality outcomes.

  • Serve as a strategic technical partner for enterprise clients: understand their roadmap and priorities, align Airwallex solutions to their goals, and proactively manage the post‑sale relationship to drive adoption, growth and retention.

  • Plan and lead regular business and technical reviews (e.g. QBRs) with the commercial owner, surfacing insights on performance, risks and opportunities – and turning them into clear action plans.

  • Own technical escalations for your accounts, providing calm, structured leadership through incidents and ensuring clear, executive‑ready communication throughout.

  • Partner closely with Account Executives and Account Managers to identify and shape expansion opportunities (upsell and cross‑sell), contributing technical insight into account plans and commercial proposals.

  • Use product usage data, commercial metrics and client health indicators to monitor account health, prioritise initiatives, and recommend strategies that improve outcomes for both customers and Airwallex.

  • Stay current on the European payments and fintech landscape (including regulations such as PSD2 and local market nuances) and translate that knowledge into practical guidance for customers.

  • Communicate complex technical concepts clearly and confidently to both technical and non‑technical stakeholders, adapting your style across cultures and audiences.

Who you are

We're looking for people who meet the minimum requirements for this role. The preferred qualifications are great to have, but are not mandatory.

Minimum qualifications:

  • 5+ years in a technical customer‑facing role (e.g. Technical Account Manager, Solutions Consultant, Technical CSM, Implementation Manager) within payments, fintech, SaaS or financial services.

  • Strong technical foundation with solid understanding of APIs, SDKs, webhooks and system integrations, and the ability to quickly grasp complex technical architectures.

  • Proven, hands‑on experience designing, implementing and supporting integrations for payment or similar financial product stacks.

  • Demonstrated track record of diagnosing and solving complex technical and operational issues, working through cross‑functional teams to drive resolution.

  • Experience acting as a trusted technical advisor to enterprise customers, including managing post‑sale relationships, leading structured reviews (e.g. QBRs) and handling high‑stakes escalations.

  • Evidence of a commercial mindset – comfortable partnering with sales and account management teams to identify and shape upsell and cross‑sell opportunities.

  • Fluency in English, with excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to clearly explain technical concepts to both engineers and senior non‑technical stakeholders.

  • Self‑starter who thrives in a fast‑paced, high‑growth environment, able to manage multiple complex accounts and willing to travel within Europe as required.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Deep domain knowledge of the European payments, fintech or financial services landscape, including familiarity with regulations such as PSD2, SEPA and major local payment methods.

  • Proficiency in at least one additional major European language (e.g. German, French, Spanish or Dutch) to support client engagement across the region.

  • Experience using data and analytics (e.g. dashboards, logs, basic querying) to monitor product usage, understand client behaviour and inform recommendations or prioritisation.

  • Background working closely with or within Product, Engineering, Compliance and Operations teams, with a track record of influencing roadmaps based on customer needs and market insights.

  • Prior experience in a scale‑up or similar high‑growth environment, with comfort navigating ambiguity and contributing to building new processes and best practices.About the team

raw.title: Associate Relationship Manager - South West
raw.description:
About Allica Bank

Allica is the UK’s fastest growing company - and the fastest-growing financial technology (Fintech) firm ever. Our purpose is to help established SMEs, one of the last major underserved opportunities in Fintech.

Established SMEs are the backbone of local communities - representing over a third of our economy - yet have been largely neglected both by traditional high street banks and modern fintech providers.

Department Description

Our vision is to reimagine Relationship Banking for established SMEs, through the very best people, products and digital tools. Allica’s Relationship Management team was formed in 2022 and continues to grow at pace, providing established SME customers with expert human relationships alongside modern banking technology.

The team supports customers with lending, current accounts, savings, asset finance and working capital facilities, while building deep local relationships with SME customers, trusted professional advisers and business communities.

The Associate Relationship Manager role is a newly created position that is a key step in our ambition to build the best Relationship team to support our SME clients. The successful candidate will manage a portfolio of clients and be expected to deliver across a range of commercial, customer service and risk objectives whilst also providing support to the wider relationship team as part of their development.

This is a great opportunity for someone looking to develop their skills and progress a career as an SME Relationship Manager.

Principal Accountabilities

  • Manage a portfolio of SME customers delivering outstanding customer service, building genuine and trusting relationships and develop a deep understanding of your clients’ businesses and their ambitions.

  • Deliver against a range of commercial targets including lending and new customer / deposit acquisition, as well as identifying and meeting a range of client needs through the provision of Allica products and services.

  • Build a trusted external network with SME advisers and the wider business community. Leverage this network to generate new business opportunities for the bank, in addition to signposting your clients to external support and advice as appropriate.

  • Ensure that Risk is managed effectively on your portfolio, with all required risk activities completed on time and to a high standard. Use customer data and internal Allica systems to identify signs of client stress and take proactive action to tackle early.

  • Work closely with a Senior Relationship Manager, contributing to building a bespoke personal development plan which will include supporting them and the wider team as part of your learning.

  • Take an active role in new business campaigns, including attending events, following up on leads, supporting prospect engagement and undertaking some cold calling where appropriate.

  • Support event organisation and follow-up activity, helping the team build strong local relationships with SME customers, prospects, accountants, solicitors and other trusted professional advisers.

  • Maintain accurate CRM records, strong follow-up discipline and good control over customer, prospect and portfolio activity.

  • Build strong, collaborative and productive relationships with your team and wider internal stakeholders to ensure customer needs are meet efficiently and any issues resolved quickly.

Personal Attributes & Experience

  • Some B2B sales, account management and/or SME banking experience, with a clear interest in building a career in SME relationship banking and a passion for supporting SMEs to be more successful.

  • Some experience of commercial lending and understanding / analysing financial accounts would be of benefit.

  • Curious, proactive and keen to learn, with the motivation to develop lending, sales, risk management and portfolio management capability through formal training and on-the-job coaching.

  • Confident engaging with customers, prospects and SME business advisers (including in person, via video call and by phone) asking great questions, following up consistently and building professional relationships.

  • Good organisation and attention to detail, with the ability to manage customer information and requests, portfolio tasks and follow-up actions accurately and at pace.

  • Practical understanding of customer service, sales activity and account management disciplines, ideally gained in a B2B, financial services or relationship-led environment.

  • Confident using systems, CRM tools and data to manage activity, track progress and support strong customer and risk outcomes.

  • Experience using AI tools in a business environment would also be of benefit.

  • An energetic, resilient, hands-on approach, with the confidence to get into the detail, solve problems and take ownership of outcomes.

  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to build credibility with customers, prospects, advisers, colleagues and stakeholders.

  • Strong alignment to Allica’s values, with the judgement, integrity and energy to lead by example and help contribute to the next phase of the Direct Relationship Management channel.

Working at Allica Bank

At Allica Bank we want to ensure our employees have the right tools and environment in which to succeed in their role and in support of our customers.

Our employees are at the heart of everything we do, so our benefits are designed with you in mind:

  • Full onboarding support and continued development opportunities

  • Options for flexible working

  • Regular social activities

  • Pension contributions

  • Discretionary bonus scheme

  • Private health cover

  • Life assurance

  • Family friendly policies including enhanced Maternity & Paternity leave

Don’t tick every box?

Don’t worry if you don’t have all the skills or requirements listed on the job description. If you think you’ll be a good fit, we’d still love to hear from you!

Flexible working

We know the ‘9-to-5’ isn’t right for everyone. That’s why Allica Bank is fully committed to flexible and hybrid working. Please let us know what is best for you and, if we can, we will do our best to accommodate.

Diversity

We’re a diverse bunch here at Allica, with all kinds of experiences, backgrounds and lifestyles. Our openness and differences make us stronger, and we want everybody to feel comfortable bringing as much of themselves to work with them as they like.

raw.title: Business Director – Moshi (Carwow Creative Agency)
raw.description:
OUR MISSION

To become the car-changing destination of choice. By combining technology, media and deep automotive expertise, we've turned how people buy, sell, advertise and lease cars on its head.

What started as a simple reviews site is now one of the largest online car-changing destinations in Europe. Last year alone we grew over 50% with nearly £3bn worth of cars bought on site, while £1.8bn of cars were listed for sale through our Sell My Car service.

In the last couple of years we have gone big and acquired both Carwow Leasey, a leasing broker and Autovia, creators of AutoExpress and Evo magazines, doubling our audience overnight. Together we now have one of the biggest YouTube channels in the world with almost 10m subscribers and over 1.1 billion annual views, while we sell 1.2 million print copies of our magazines and have an annual web content reach over 350million. We also launched our successful Sell My Car business in Germany. We are continually driving to make Carwow the go-to destination for people looking to change their car.

Role Overview

The Growth & Proposition Lead (TBC NAME) will lead the commercial growth and strategic positioning of Moshi, Carwow’s in-house creative agency serving OEM partners.

This is a senior leadership role responsible for driving revenue, owning key OEM relationships and embedding Moshi as a core part of Carwow’s commercial proposition across markets. The role will bridge commercial, creative and production teams to ensure Moshi delivers high-impact, scalable creative solutions that drive measurable value for OEM partners.

The Business Director will also play a critical role in shaping Moshi’s operating model, ensuring the agency is structured for growth with clear processes, strong client service and efficient delivery.

Key Responsibilities

1. Commercial Ownership & Revenue Growth

• Own Moshi’s revenue performance and growth trajectory across all markets

• Identify and unlock new revenue opportunities across:

Creative campaigns

Always-on content

Product launches

Strategic content partnerships

• Partner with Carwow commercial leadership to embed Moshi into OEM deals and co-funded activity

• Drive revenue diversification beyond one-off projects into longer-term, higher-margin partnerships

• Build clear commercial frameworks (pricing, packaging, margin discipline)

2. OEM Client Leadership

• Own senior relationships with OEM marketing stakeholders across key accounts

• Position Moshi as a strategic creative partner, not a production vendor

• Lead:

Brief development

Creative solutioning

Proposal creation

Pitch presentations

• Translate OEM business objectives into effective creative and content strategies

• Ensure high levels of client satisfaction, retention and upsell

3. Pipeline Development & Business Development

• Build and manage a robust Moshi pipeline across all markets

• Work closely with Carwow commercial teams (UK, Germany, Spain) to:

Identify opportunities within existing OEM partnerships

Introduce Moshi into early-stage commercial conversations

• Lead proactive outreach and proposal development

• Convert:

One-off campaigns → repeat engagements

Repeat engagements → strategic retainers / partnerships

4. Operational Structure & Delivery Oversight

• Establish scalable delivery processes to support Moshi growth

• Improve:

Resource planning and utilisation

Project workflow and timelines

Cross-market coordination

• Work closely with creative and production teams to:

Ensure high-quality output

Maintain delivery efficiency

Protect margins

• Introduce clear reporting on project performance (delivery, profitability, client outcomes)

5. Team Leadership & Capability Building

• Lead and develop Moshi’s client services and delivery teams

• Define a clear operating structure aligned to growth ambitions

• Build capability across:

Client servicing

Commercial thinking

Creative strategy

• Foster a high-performance culture focused on:

Accountability

Quality

Commercial outcomes

Key Success Metrics

  • Moshi revenue growth (YoY and vs target)

  • Contribution to overall Carwow OEM revenue

  • Pipeline value and conversion rates

  • Client retention and expansion (share of wallet)

  • Project profitability and margin improvement

  • Delivery performance (on time, on budget, quality)

Skills & Experience

• Significant experience in a senior commercial or client leadership role within a creative/media/agency environment

• Proven track record of driving revenue growth and managing senior client relationships

• Strong understanding of:

Brand and performance marketing

Content and creative production

Automotive / OEM marketing (preferred)

• Experience building pipelines, leading pitches and converting strategic partnerships

• Strong commercial acumen with ability to balance creativity and profitability

• Experience working across multiple markets and cross-functional teams

Personal Attributes

  • Commercially driven and outcome-focused

  • Credible at senior OEM stakeholder level

  • Strategic thinker with hands-on execution capability

  • Strong communicator and storyteller

  • Able to operate in a fast-paced, scaling environment

  • High ownership mentality with a bias for action

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • 30-minute virtual Introductory call with our Talent team

  • 45-minute virtual Hiring Manager interview

  • Take-home exercise, followed by a 1.5-hour onsite interview

  • Virtual Values interview with key senior stakeholders


WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU

  • Competitive comp package

  • 28 days' holiday plus bank holidays, increasing to 35 with length of service, plus extras for house moves, weddings and more!

  • Employee-friendly share options

  • Pension scheme via Royal London - up to 5% company contribution

  • Vitality private healthcare insurance

  • Life Assurance - 4x annual salary

  • Monthly coaching sessions with Spill - our mental wellbeing partner

  • Inclusive parental, partner and shared parental leave, including up to 20 weeks' full pay maternity and shared parental leave, and 8 weeks' full partner pay, as well as fertility treatment and pregnancy loss policies

  • Bubble childcare support and discounted nanny fees for little ones

  • 'Work from abroad for a month' annual scheme

  • Generous learning and development budget

  • £500/€550 home office budget

Diversity and inclusion is an integral part of our culture. We know that diverse teams are strong teams, so we welcome those with alternative identities, backgrounds, and experiences to apply for this position. We make recruiting decisions based on experience, skills and potential, so all our applicants are treated fairly and equally.

raw.title: Head of GTM & Revenue Operations
raw.description:
THE CARWOW GROUP

Carwow Group is driven by a passion for getting people into cars. But not just any car, the right car. That’s why we are building the go-to destination for car-changing, whether you are looking to buy, sell or lease. Designed to reach drivers everywhere with our trail-blazing portfolio of personality rich automotive brands; Carwow, Auto Express, evo, Driving Electric and Car Buyer.

What started as a simple reviews site, is now one of the largest online car-changing destinations in Europe. Last year alone we grew over 50% with nearly £3bn worth of cars bought on site, while £1.8bn of cars were listed for sale through our Sell My Car service. Over 10m customers have used Carwow to help them buy and sell cars since its inception.

In 2024 we went big and acquired Autovia, doubling our audience overnight. Together we now have one of the biggest YouTube channels in the world with over 1.1 billion annual views, sell 1.2 million print copies of our magazines and have an annual web content reach over 350million.

WHY JOIN US?

We are winners of the prestigious Culture 100 award that recognises the most loved and happiest tech companies to work for! We have just raised $52m in funding led by global venture capital firm Bessemer Venture Partners (an early backer of LinkedIn and Shopify) to accelerate our growth plans!

As pioneers, we’re always driving for new territory and positive change, so our work as a group is never done. Where others see difficulty, it’s our responsibility to see possibility – building new experiences, launching new titles and listening to drivers.

Being a part of Carwow Group means championing drivers and the automotive industry, acting as a disrupter and never being afraid to fail (but learning fast when we do!).

Our team of 600 employees across the UK, Germany, Spain and Portugal are revolutionising car-changing and we are fast expanding our mission across every single brand and country we operate in, so jump in!


THE ROLE

Carwow has just brought its Sell My Car and Get Your Car commercial teams together into one team serving one dealer network. Those dealers buy cars from drivers through Sell My Car and sell cars to drivers through Get Your Car. As Head of GTM & Revenue Operations, you'll design how that team runs: the process, the tooling, the analytics and forecast the business trades on, and the automation that takes the admin away from the day-to-day. The commercial number here depends on how dealers behave on our marketplace each day as much as on the sales pipeline, so this is RevOps with more moving parts than most, and a rare chance to build it from close to the ground up.

The commercial team is around 60 people today, working alongside around 100 in operations, and we plan to scale our commercial operation significantly next year. You'll start with a small team and a clear mandate to build the function the business needs, making the case for investment with the VP's support. There's real room to grow, for the team and for you.

You report to the VP, Marketplace Operations, and you're accountable for the commercial forecast, the sales process and the Salesforce roadmap. The commercial teams own the selling and the relationships and the tech org builds and runs the platform; you work closely with all of them. After a year, success looks like a forecast the business trusts and trades on, one Salesforce and one process across both products, and a clear read of where deals are lost so enablement aims at the right things.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

Working with the commercial organisation, sales leadership, workforce management, the trading leads and the central analytics and data teams, you will:

  • Design the operating model: one go-to-market process, pipeline and dealer view across Sell My Car and Get Your Car, with the capacity and headcount plan to match, built with Workforce Management.

  • Shape targets, comp and territories: design them with commercial leadership so each person's number ties to the business outcome.

  • Own the forecast: build a forward-looking commercial forecast on marketplace and pipeline drivers that feeds trading, reconciles to Finance, and gives leadership a clear weekly view of where the number is heading.

  • Own the Salesforce roadmap: one platform for the whole commercial team, with the workflows, sales-engagement tooling and dashboards people actually use, delivered with the tech org.

  • Build in AI and automation from the start: take manual work out of forecasting, reporting and the commercial teams' day, so they spend their time with dealers.

  • Find where performance is lost: use the data to diagnose where reps and teams fall short, from ramp time to call quality to lost deals, agree with sales leadership where training should focus, and measure whether it worked.

  • Build the team and run change: hire and shape the function, and run the commercial PMO so cross-functional programmes land on time with clear owners.


WHAT YOU’LL NEED

Please note: We know that no candidate will be a perfect match for everything here, so please apply if you're close to the brief. If you meet most of the essentials, we'd like to hear from you.

The essentials:

  • You've led a revenue-operations, commercial-operations or GTM-operations team in a marketplace, growth or B2B sales business

  • You've built a forecast that leadership relied on, and you can explain what drove it when it missed

  • You know Salesforce well as a system of record: you can shape the data model and process, and work with a platform team to deliver it

  • You've designed targets, comp, territories and capacity plans that tie to business outcomes

  • You've grown a team from a small base, hired well and set a clear bar

How you'll work (we'll explore these in interview):

  • Credible with senior people: you make a well-evidenced case, hold it under challenge, and raise the hard truth early

  • Fluent with AI: you use it to work faster and help a team adopt it

Nice to have:

  • Marketplace, two-sided platform or automotive experience

  • Hands-on Salesforce admin or certification, SQL, and sales-engagement tooling such as Groove or Outreach

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Phone screen with a member of the Talent Team

  • First round interview with the hiring manager focussed on prior experience

  • Second round made up of a case study presentation on a revenue-operations problem (we'll send the brief in advance and give you time to prepare)

  • Situational/company values interview with senior members of the leadership team

  • Final round interview with a member of the Exec team

We want everyone to do their best thinking, so if you'd like any adjustments to the process, just let us know.

WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU

  • Hybrid working: 3 days a week in the office, 2 remote

  • Competitive salary

  • Matched pension contributions

  • Matched pension contributions for a peaceful retirement

  • Share options - when we thrive, so do you!

  • Vitality Private Healthcare, for peace of mind, plus eyecare vouchers

  • Life Assurance for (even more) peace of mind

  • Monthly coaching sessions with Spill - our mental wellbeing partner

  • 28 days annual leave plus bank holidays, rising to 30 days after 3 years and 35 after 10 years, with the option to buy 3 additional days

  • 1 day of leave for your wedding, and 1 day when you move house

  • Work from abroad for a month

  • Inclusive parental, partner and shared parental leave, plus fertility treatment and pregnancy loss support

THE OPPORTUNITY

Millions of people come to Carwow when they are ready to change their car. That is some of the highest-intent automotive audience in the UK, and it makes Carwow one of the most valuable places for dealers and manufacturers to reach buyers at the moment of decision. Retail media is how we turn that intent into revenue, for our partners and for the business.

We have built the foundations: sponsored placements across the buying journey, a growing media and audience offering, and commercial products for dealers and manufacturers. Demand is ahead of what we can currently serve. If we can make our advertising products smarter, more relevant and easier to buy, we grow revenue for partners while keeping the experience useful for the consumer. That balance is the job.

This role is the product voice for retail media: setting the direction for what we build and working day to day with engineering, design, data and commercial teams to build it.

This is also a moment where AI changes what's possible. Advertisers want smarter targeting, better recommendations on where to spend, and proof of what worked. We want to build those things. The PM in this role will need the curiosity to explore what that could look like, and the rigour to distinguish genuine value from noise.

If you know retail media inside out, want to shape a fast-growing revenue line, and build things with a direct line to commercial outcomes, this is it.

 

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

  • Product Strategy & Execution:

  • Cross-functional Leadership:

    • Communicate strategy and trade-offs clearly to leadership and stakeholders, written as well as verbal

    • Support the commercial team in partner conversations where product context matters: capability deep-dives, roadmap discussions, strategic accounts

  • Proven retail media experience is a prerequisite: you have built or owned sponsored ads, onsite media or audience products at a marketplace, retailer or ad tech business, and you know how the industry works

  • 5+ years of product management experience, with evidence of growing advertising revenue or advertiser performance

  • Technically strong: you understand ad serving, targeting, auction and pricing mechanics, APIs and tracking, and can hold a credible conversation with engineers about architecture and trade-offs

  • Comfortable with data: you interrogate performance data yourself, design your own tests, and form your own hypotheses rather than waiting for analysis to land in your inbox

raw.description:
About us:

Causaly is redefining how humans acquire knowledge and develop insights in biomedicine. Our AI-powered platform enables researchers and decision-makers to discover and interpret evidence from millions of scientific publications, clinical trials, regulatory documents, and other complex data sources in minutes.

We are building the world’s most advanced biomedical knowledge platform, powered by a high-precision Knowledge Graph and GenAI capabilities. Our technology is already used by leading biopharmaceutical organizations to accelerate drug discovery, improve safety, and drive better decision-making.

Backed by top-tier investors including ICONIQ, Index Ventures, Pentech, and Marathon, we are scaling rapidly and expanding our product suite and market presence. 

About the Role

We are hiring a Director of People to take full ownership of People Operations and Employee Experience at Causaly, for 100 to 125 people across the UK, Greece, the US and other European countries, including remote employees through employer-of-record providers. You will run contracts, payroll, benefits, compliance, HR systems and employee relations, and shape how people experience working here from day one.

You will lead and develop a team of two People Operations Associates, 1x in London and 1x in Athens, and work closely with our leadership team and Finance, with the autonomy to set priorities and the accountability to deliver them. This role does not currently include Talent Acquisition, which sits in a separate team.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the People Operations roadmap and the full employee lifecycle, from contracts and onboarding to offboarding, including contractors and third-party suppliers.

  • Work closely with our Senior Talent Partner on hiring, offers and onboarding.

  • Oversee payroll and benefits across our UK, Greece and US entities with Finance, and manage our employer-of-record providers for remote employees.

  • Own employment law compliance in every country we operate in, including right to work and visas, and keep our policies, handbooks and contracts current, with our General Counsel and local advisers.

  • Own our HRIS and People data, keep it accurate and compliant, and produce reporting leaders can act on.

  • Manage employee relations cases end to end, including investigations, grievances and exits, with our General Counsel and external counsel, and coach managers through difficult conversations.

  • Lead our compensation review and performance and development (P&D) cycles end to end, working with Finance and leadership.

  • Own learning and development, including our development budget and programmes for managers and teams.

  • Partner with the Finance Director and COO on People strategy and workforce planning as we grow.

  • Shape the employee experience across all locations and for remote colleagues, including engagement surveys, communications, wellbeing and office culture.

  • Own our London, Athens and New York offices and facilities, setting standards and managing landlords, suppliers, budget and health and safety, with your team covering London and Athens, local providers covering New York, and you hands-on where it matters.

  • Use AI and automation to remove manual work from People processes, and put the right tools in place.

What We’re Looking For

  • Experience leading People Operations at Head of level, or equivalent, in a venture-backed tech or SaaS scale-up, ideally of 100 to 300 people.

  • Hands-on payroll and benefits experience across the UK, US and other European countries, including through employer-of-record providers, and owning an HRIS, with strong attention to detail.

  • Strong UK employment law knowledge and experience supporting employees in another country.

  • Sound judgement and discretion on complex employee relations matters.

  • Credibility and communication skills to influence senior leaders and managers.

  • Confidence with data, reporting and budget conversations with Finance.

  • Experience managing a small team, ideally including someone based in another country.

  • A pragmatic, low-ego operator who enjoys building process and getting into the detail.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with Greek or wider EU employment practices; CIPD Level 7 or an equivalent qualification.

Benefits

💰 Competitive compensation package

🩺 Private medical & dental insurance

📔 Life insurance (4 x salary)

🤓 Personal development budget

🧘 Individual wellbeing budget

🌴 25 days holiday plus bank holidays

🥳 Your birthday off!

🚀 Potential to have real impact and accelerated career growth as a member of an international team that's building a transformative AI product.

raw.description:
About us:

Causaly is redefining how humans acquire knowledge and develop insights in biomedicine. Our AI-powered platform enables researchers and decision-makers to discover and interpret evidence from millions of scientific publications, clinical trials, regulatory documents, and other complex data sources in minutes.

We are building the world’s most advanced biomedical knowledge platform, powered by a high-precision Knowledge Graph and GenAI capabilities. Our technology is already used by leading biopharmaceutical organizations to accelerate drug discovery, improve safety, and drive better decision-making.

Backed by top-tier investors including ICONIQ, Index Ventures, Pentech, and Marathon, we are scaling rapidly and expanding our product suite and market presence. 

About the Role

Causaly is hiring a Strategy and Solutions Lead to incubate and validate new growth opportunities at the intersection of AI, data, product, and our pharma and biotech customers across R&D and commercial functions.

This role focuses exclusively on new territory — new capabilities, solution lines, integrations, or market segments — where customer demand goes beyond what our product supports out of the box. The mandate is to turn ambiguous enterprise demand into scalable, repeatable solution plays grounded in real pharma workflows, drive executive decision-making, and then hand those plays into BAU teams once validated.

You will work directly with Causaly’s executive leadership and lead discussions with senior stakeholders across pharma R&D and commercial functions, as well as their data and technology teams, to shape strategic partnerships, solution architecture, and product decisions. You will operate with significant autonomy, owning opportunities from the first strategic conversation through to executive decision and handoff.

What You’ll Do

Own strategic “new territory” decisions

◆ Own intake and shaping of strategic enterprise opportunities that require new capabilities, integrations, packaging, or market positioning.

◆ Drive executive decisioning on whether to pursue, park, or decline opportunities, with clear rationale, options, and business and technical implications.

◆ Maintain a clear boundary between incubation work and BAU; ensure this team is only engaged where something new must be created.

Lead senior R&D and commercial conversations and translate demand into scalable solution paths

◆ Lead high-stakes discussions with senior stakeholders across pharma R&D (e.g. Discovery, Translational Science, Clinical Development) and commercial functions (e.g. Portfolio Strategy, New Product Planning, Medical Affairs, Market Access).

◆ Ground discovery in customers’ end-to-end workflows and decision points (e.g. target identification and validation, Target Product Profile development, candidate selection, indication expansion, lifecycle management) to define target state, success criteria, and constraints.

◆ Translate ambiguous asks into a solution concept and delivery path, including where Causaly creates value in the workflow, scope boundaries, sequencing, timelines, risks, dependencies, and mutual commitments.

◆ Shape expectations and commercial framing to ensure scalable commitments (what is standard, what is configurable, what requires investment, and what is out of scope).

Design and steer technical solutions

◆ Work with customer architecture, data, IT, and AI teams in working-level depth on Causaly’s platform capabilities, APIs, data model, and integration patterns (e.g. with internal data lakes, knowledge management systems, and enterprise AI tooling), going beyond high-level positioning to a solution design both sides can build against.

◆ Drive the solution design for new plays, including integration approach, data flows, security, and deployment model, and work alongside Causaly’s Engineering and Data teams through build, testing, and deployment, without being the engineer writing production code.

◆ Pressure-test technical feasibility early: review architectures, spot integration and data risks, and make informed calls on what can be configured, what needs to be built, and what effort it will take.

◆ Shape and evaluate technology partnerships (e.g. data providers, cloud and AI platforms, systems integrators), including strategic rationale, technical fit, integration approach, and joint solution design.

◆ Represent Causaly’s platform and roadmap credibly in executive and technical forums, clearly positioning what the platform does today, what is configurable, and where it is heading.

Build repeatable solution playbooks (incl. Private Data & integrations)

◆ Turn recurring demand into solution playbooks anchored in specific R&D and commercial workflows, including:

◇ Offering definition, use cases, and packaging

◇ Qualification and fit criteria

◇ Scoping templates and success plans

◇ Delivery blueprints, reference architectures, and enablement assets

◆ Standardise complex offerings (e.g. Private Data, enterprise integrations, and AI workflows on customer data) into productised motions with clear patterns, governance, and pilot-to-rollout pathways.

◆ Partner with Product, Engineering, and Data to define feasibility options and reference architectures, and surface clear product and investment recommendations.

Validate plays through lighthouse execution

◆ Co-sponsor a small number of lighthouse opportunities with Sales to validate new solution plays.

◆ Orchestrate early cross-functional work (pilot design, governance, decisioning) with the explicit goal of making the play transferable and repeatable, not owning delivery long-term.

Institutionalise and hand off into BAU

◆ Drive clean handoff of validated plays into BAU (Sales, CS, Delivery, Product), including training, assets, decision trees, and ownership clarity.

◆ Maintain a structured feedback loop into Product on product candidates, investment needs, and learned constraints from enterprise demand.

What We’re Looking For

◆ 7+ years’ experience at the intersection of pharma or life sciences strategy, AI and data, and enterprise customers, with a track record of leading discussions with senior R&D and commercial stakeholders and shaping ambiguous asks into scalable solutions.

◆ Strong fit from one of the following backgrounds:

◇ Life science strategy or AI consulting at Engagement Manager / Associate Partner level, with substantial R&D or commercial work and ownership of AI or data programmes from strategy through to scale-up

◇ Enterprise Solutions / Solutions Strategy roles in B2B SaaS serving pharma and biotech, particularly in AI-, data-, or platform-heavy products

◆ Deep understanding of end-to-end pharma R&D and commercial workflows and the decisions within them (e.g. target identification, Target Product Profile, candidate selection, indication expansion, launch and lifecycle planning), and of how data and AI can change them.

◆ Hands-on experience building, deploying, and/or integrating technology solutions in enterprise settings (e.g. data platforms, AI and LLM applications, API and system integrations). You have been close enough to the build to understand how a solution works, not just what it does, and have seen solutions through to production.

◆ Ability to read and challenge solution architectures, reason through data pipelines, APIs, and integration patterns, and understand how AI and LLM systems are built and evaluated (e.g. retrieval-augmented generation, agentic workflows, knowledge graphs).

◆ Experience turning complex, bespoke-seeming enterprise demand into repeatable playbooks (qualification criteria, scoping frameworks, pilot design, and BAU handoff).

◆ Strong judgement in making and defending pursue / park / decline recommendations based on product direction, feasibility, scalability, and business impact.

◆ Comfort driving executive decisioning (internally and on the customer side) across Product, Engineering, and GTM, and translating technical trade-offs into clear business choices.

Nice to Have

◆ Scientific or quantitative background (e.g. advanced degree in life sciences, engineering, or a related field).

◆ Experience on AI or GenAI programmes in pharma, from use-case definition through to scaled deployment.

◆ Prior experience in a technical capacity (e.g. forward deployed engineer, data scientist, software engineer, technical product manager).

◆ Familiarity with enterprise data governance in regulated environments (e.g. GxP, data privacy, information security reviews).

◆ Exposure to market expansion, new segment GTM, technology partnerships, or solution incubation.

We are on a mission to accelerate scientific breakthroughs for ALL humankind, and we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. raw.title: Regional Sales Director
raw.description:
Job Title: Regional Sales Director, Private Sector (Financial Services), NEMEA

Location: London, United Kingdom

The Chainalysis Private Sector team helps financial services organizations understand blockchain activity, manage financial crime risk, and adopt digital assets with confidence. Across NEMEA, we work with banks, fintechs, payments businesses, and digital asset companies to address compliance, fraud, and investigation needs. Our sales team partners with specialists across the business to connect customer priorities with the right blockchain intelligence solutions.

As Regional Sales Director, you lead and develop the Private Sector Financial Services sales team across NEMEA from London. You own the regional sales strategy and revenue performance, combining disciplined execution with hands-on support for complex enterprise deals. You build senior customer relationships and help the team translate financial crime challenges and digital asset opportunities into clear business value. You create an accountable, collaborative environment where sales executives develop their skills and consistently deliver results.

In this role, you'll:

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of sales executives to meet and exceed individual and regional revenue targets.

  • Define and execute the NEMEA financial services sales strategy, prioritizing markets, customer segments, and accounts based on opportunity and customer needs.

  • Own regional bookings and annual recurring revenue targets, balancing new customer acquisition with expansion across existing accounts.

  • Build qualified pipeline through account planning, targeted prospecting, and coordinated engagement with Marketing, Sales Development, and partners.

  • Guide complex enterprise sales cycles from discovery through negotiation and close, engaging compliance, fraud, risk, investigations, technology, procurement, and executive stakeholders.

  • Build relationships with senior financial services decision-makers and help customers connect blockchain intelligence to their business objectives.

  • Maintain accurate forecasts and Salesforce records, using pipeline reviews and sales activity data to identify risks and coach the team.

  • Partner with Solutions Engineering, Product, Customer Success, and other specialists to develop customer solutions, support adoption, and identify expansion opportunities.

  • Stay current on digital asset adoption, financial crime trends, and relevant UK and European regulatory developments to inform account strategies and customer conversations.

  • Recruit and onboard sales executives, establish clear expectations, and build a collaborative team culture across the region.


We're looking for candidates who have:

  • 7+ years of enterprise B2B SaaS sales experience, including at least 3 years leading and developing quota-carrying sales teams.

  • A record of meeting or exceeding multimillion annual recurring revenue targets in complex, consultative sales environments.

  • Experience selling technology or data solutions to financial services organizations, including banks, fintechs, or payments businesses.

  • Experience engaging compliance, financial crime, fraud, risk, or investigations teams and translating their needs into a business case.

  • Experience leading sales across multiple markets, with an understanding of the UK and broader NEMEA financial services landscape.

  • Demonstrated ability to coach sales executives, recruit talent, and manage performance against clear goals.

  • Strong executive communication and negotiation skills, with experience managing complex procurement processes and multiple decision-makers.

  • Proficiency in Salesforce and sales analytics, with a disciplined approach to pipeline management, forecasting, and account planning.


Nice to have experience:

  • Experience selling blockchain intelligence, financial crime analytics, fraud prevention, or RegTech solutions.

  • Knowledge of digital assets, stablecoins, and blockchain use cases in banking and payments.

  • Familiarity with UK digital asset regulation, EU MiCA requirements, AML/KYC obligations, and FATF guidance.

  • An established network of financial services relationships across EMEA, additional regional language skills, or experience developing partner-led opportunities.

 
 

About Chainalysis

Blockchain technology is powering a growing wave of innovation. Businesses and governments around the world are using blockchains to make banking more efficient, connect with their customers, and investigate criminal cases. As adoption of blockchain technology grows, more and more organizations seek access to all this ecosystem has to offer. That’s where Chainalysis comes in. We provide complete knowledge of what’s happening on blockchains through our data, services, and solutions. With Chainalysis, organizations can navigate blockchains safely and with confidence.

You belong here.

At Chainalysis, we believe that diversity of experience and thought makes us stronger. With both customers and employees around the world, we are committed to ensuring our team reflects the unique communities around us. Some of the ways we’re ensuring we keep learning are an internal Diversity Committee, Days of Reflection throughout the year including International Women’s Day, Harvey Milk Day, World Humanitarian Day, and UN International Migrants Day, and a commitment to continue revisiting and reevaluating our diversity culture.

We encourage applicants across any race, ethnicity, gender/gender expression, age, spirituality, ability, experience and more. Additionally, if you need any accommodations to make our interview process more accessible to you due to a disability, don't hesitate to let us know. You can learn more here. We can’t wait to meet you.

AI at Chainalysis
AI is not a feature at Chainalysis - it is a new way of working. One that turns instructions into work done, and helps us move faster than the threats we're built to counter, and we expect our employees to take ownership of the output and ensure quality. As the world's most trusted blockchain analytics platform, Chainalysis sits at a rare intersection of proprietary data, regulatory relationships and crypto expertise that makes it uniquely placed to shape and lead the next era of AI-driven intelligence - and we expect everyone here, regardless of role, to be an active part of it.

AI fluency is tied directly to how we measure performance and how we plan to win. There is no substitute for your own curiosity. We provide the tools, workflows, and space to experiment - but the expectation is that you develop these capabilities yourself, bring ideas, and collaborate across teams to reinvent the way work gets done. We are not using AI to do less. We are using it to do what was never possible before.

About Chainalysis

Chainalysis is the blockchain data platform, making it easy to connect the movement of digital assets to real-world services. Powered by deep blockchain data and AI, organizations can investigate illicit activity, manage risk exposure, and develop innovative market solutions built on the industry's most trusted blockchain intelligence. Our mission is to build trust in blockchains, blending safety and security with an unwavering commitment to growth and innovation.

You belong here. 

At Chainalysis, we believe that diversity of experience and thought makes us stronger. With both customers and employees around the world, we are committed to ensuring our team reflects the unique communities around us. We’re ensuring we keep learning by committing to continually revisit and reevaluate our diversity culture.

We encourage applicants across any race, ethnicity, gender/gender expression, age, spirituality, ability, experience and more. If you need any accommodations to make our interview process more accessible to you due to a disability, don't hesitate to let us know. You can learn more here. We can’t wait to meet you.

About Us

Condukt is the next-generation compliance platform for financial services, offering an agentic solution powered by real-time data for business identity.

Always-on and policy-aware, Condukt enables financial institutions and fintechs to gain actionable insights into business verification - unlocking growth, increasing efficiency, and strengthening compliance.

We were founded by former operators and builders with deep experience in banking, payments, and lending. Today, our team spans across London and Porto, bringing together engineers, product owners, and operators from companies like Revolut, Meta, Block (Square), SumUp, American Express, Yandex, and OakNorth.

Trusted by leading regulated entities, including Wise, Tide, Mollie, Shift4, Flatpay, and myPOS, Condukt is backed by top investors, including Lightspeed Venture Partners and MMC Ventures.

 

Position Overview

We’re looking for a Senior Compliance Consultant to help our clients navigate regulatory change, horizon-scan upcoming regulation, and overcome regulatory challenges so they can transform their businesses and meet their strategic growth objectives.

This is a versatile, high-impact role at the intersection of regulation, client advisory, practical delivery and product strategy. Your mission is to deeply understand our clients’ needs and regulatory obligations, and to deliver solutions that help them achieve their compliance and business outcomes. You’ll stay ahead of the risk and compliance landscape, translating regulatory change into clear guidance for our customers and concrete requirements for our Product team.

Whether you’re shaping a client’s regulatory strategy or influencing our product roadmap, you’ll bring deep knowledge and hands-on experience of financial crime compliance, along with strong commercial awareness. Acting as an in-house consultant, you’ll connect long-term regulatory horizons with granular operational realities.

 

As an early-stage, fast-growing company, we value people who take ownership, move comfortably between complex challenges, and have the judgement to turn them into sharp, practical solutions. You’ll also work on long-horizon strategic projects, such as building government relationships and expanding Condukt’s global data footprint, where progress is measured in weeks, not months.

If you thrive in dynamic environments where no two days look the same, enjoy tackling a constant stream of new and complex problems, and want to help shape how financial institutions and fintechs approach compliance, this role is for you.

 

What you’ll do:

  • Act as Condukt’s subject matter expert on KYB/KYC and AML/CFT, giving clients clear, commercially minded advice on their regulatory obligations

  • Lead client engagements end to end, from understanding the business challenge and assessing current controls to designing solutions that combine Condukt’s platform with third-party providers and supporting their implementation

  • Produce high-quality, client-ready deliverables, such as gap analyses, risk assessments, onboarding and monitoring frameworks, policies and decision papers

  • Run workshops with client stakeholders, from compliance teams to the C-suite, turning discussion into practical next steps

  • Horizon-scan regulation across the UK, Europe and beyond, and brief clients on what’s coming and what it means for them, directly or alongside our commercial team

  • Build and maintain relationships with regulators, government bodies and company registers to secure access to data, expand Condukt’s global footprint and represent Condukt in industry forums

  • Shape Condukt’s advisory proposition, identifying emerging client needs and opportunities to bring new capabilities to existing clients alongside our commercial team

  • Partner with Product to translate regulatory and client needs into the signals, data and capabilities we build

  • Contribute to business development and thought leadership with a clear, well-argued point of view on regulation, through proposals, client pitches, whitepapers, briefings, webinars and industry events

  • 4+ years’ experience in financial crime compliance, gained in a consultancy, a regulator or a regulated financial services firm

  • Deep domain expertise in risk and compliance, ideally across KYB/KYC, AML/CFT or business onboarding in financial services

  • A track record of advising financial institutions and fintechs on risk, compliance or regulatory matters, with a toolkit of structured frameworks you can adapt to a fast-growing company

  • Experience leading client engagements and producing polished, client-ready deliverables

  • Experience advising on vendor assessment and selection, including running or contributing to RFP processes

You'll work with a team that has helped launch airlines and put satellites into orbit, and with an aviation advisory board whose members have run major aircraft OEMs, led airworthiness at Gulfstream, and overseen training facilities that educate a quarter of all aircraft mechanics in the US.

The role

As a Deployment Strategist, you’ll own customer implementation end-to-end.

You’ll translate complex operational requirements into AI-solutions, work hands-on with customers to drive adoption, and turn what you learn in the field into sales and engineering priorities.

This is a highly hands-on, high-ownership role. You’ll spend time in our office with the team, but also on-site with customers in hangars, maintenance facilities, and manufacturing environments, around the world. You’ll work directly with technicians, operators, managers, and executives to understand their workflows, deploy Fleetcraft into live environments, and make sure the product becomes mission-critical.

What we're looking for

We’re looking for someone with exceptional learning velocity, commercial instinct, and technical competence. You should be pragmatic, intentional, and very structured. Aerospace experience is not required - the ability to learn quickly, adapt, and handle complex implementations with high emotional intelligence.

You should be technically fluent enough to understand AI and software systems and commercially curious enough to understand what drives customer value.

  • 2+ years in consulting, technical implementation, solutions engineering, or customer-facing roles in enterprise B2B.

  • AI-native: You already use AI extensively in your work, experiment constantly, and instinctively find ways to move faster with it.

  • Technically fluent: You can hold your own with engineers and translate customer needs into actionable engineering requirements.

  • High emotional intelligence: Equally comfortable earning the trust of CEOs, IT directors, senior engineers, aircraft technicians, and pilots.

  • Structured and resourceful: Able to manage multiple deployments, solve complex problems, and bring clarity to ambiguous situations.

  • Bias to action: You take ownership, learn quickly, and prioritise getting things done over perfect plans.

What we offer

£75k–£110k salary plus meaningful early-stage equity.

A small, high-trust team where your decisions move the whole company forward. Relocation support if needed. Modern tools, real-world impact in a regulated industry, and the chance to define how AI transforms aerospace from the ground up.

If you're energised by building production AI systems that solve hard, real-world problems - and you want the ownership and pace that only comes from being early at something important, we'd love to talk.
