raw.title: Senior Backend Engineer
raw.description:
AI is being run everywhere, by humans and agents. Harmonic Security governs all of it. The AI Governance and Control (AIGC) platform understands user / agent intent and data context in real time, giving security teams visibility and control across every tool and workflow so companies can move faster with AI while minimizing risk.

We operate in one of the fastest-moving spaces in tech: the emerging intersection of AI and cybersecurity. It's a market still being defined, and we're among the first to build natively for it - protecting sensitive data in real time, at the endpoint, with minimal friction for the teams using it. Enterprises get full visibility and control. Their people get to innovate without guardrails slowing them down.

Named to the Rising in Cyber 2026 list, Harmonic is gaining serious recognition and serious traction. We're led by deep cybersecurity expertise and backed by investors who know the space: N47, Ten Eleven Ventures, and In-Q-Tel.

As AI adoption inside the enterprise accelerates, the ability to safely observe, control, and enforce policy in real time isn't a nice-to-have. It's mission-critical infrastructure. That's what we build.

How We Work: AI-First by Design

Harmonic exists to help enterprises adopt AI safely and at scale. We hold ourselves to that same standard. Everyone here actively leverages AI tools to perform their best work — from deep research and writing to building robust processes and automating complex workflows. We expect every new hire to bring a genuine curiosity for AI and a commitment to using it to work smarter, faster, and with greater creativity.

For some, this involves tinkering and remaining open to emerging tools; for others, it means architecting entirely new systems with AI at the core. We will be transparent about expectations for every role and provide the tools and support needed for you to thrive.

About the Team

Our Product Delivery team is the engine that turns vision into impact. We ship early and often, getting valuable features into the hands of customers quickly and iterating from there. We work in the open by default, sharing progress and ideas, and we trust each other to own outcomes. We’re a small but mighty crew where every person plays a critical role and we’re committed to using AI to work smarter and faster.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Backend Engineer who has an appreciation for all things security and system interconnectivity. This is a very hands-on technical role where you will be responsible for designing, building and maintaining scalable integrations between our core applications, identity providers and data security platforms.

What You'll Do

  • Own deliveries and features from start to finish

  • Design, build, and own backend services in a microservices-based, event-driven architecture

  • Implement core domain logic that drives key product workflows and system behavior

  • Ingest and process high-volume usage and event data from customer-facing endpoints

  • Build backend services that support operational, analytics, and reporting use cases

  • Model, persist, and manage domain data, enabling querying, filtering, and lifecycle management

  • Expose well-designed APIs and webhooks consumed by customers, UIs, and external systems

  • Power customer-facing UI experiences by providing backend APIs for visibility, analytics, and configuration

What You Bring

  • 3–5+ years of professional software engineering experience building backend services and distributed systems in the Java ecosystem (Java, Spring Boot, Maven/Gradle)

  • Strong understanding of event-driven architectures, asynchronous processing patterns, messaging systems, and distributed system design

  • Proven experience designing and maintaining RESTful APIs, web hooks, and service-to-service integrations

  • Comfortable operating in AWS, GCP, or Azure environments and working with modern observability tooling, logging, and monitoring platforms

  • A track record of delivering performant, reliable and scalable applications

  • Excellent collaboration and communication skills in cross-functional teams

You Might Be a Fit if You

  • Have experience building products in cybersecurity, identity, governance, compliance, data protection, or enterprise SaaS environments

  • You understand not just how to build systems, but why architectural decisions matter

  • You can balance scalability, reliability, maintainability, and speed of execution

  • You think critically about security, observability, and operational excellence from day one

  • Love the idea of blending software development, distributed systems and data-intensive applications

  • Strong familiarity with authentication and identity technologies such as OAuth, OpenID Connect (OIDC), SAML, SCIM, Entra ID (Azure AD), Okta, or other enterprise identity providers

  • Thrive in fast-paced startup environments where ambiguity is the norm

  • Enjoy shaping culture and engineering practices, not just writing code

  • Leverage AI tools as an engineer to help you build smarter, faster and better

Why Join Us

This isn't just a job - it's a chance to help define a category. Harmonic Security was named to the Rising in Cyber 2026 list, and we're just getting started. We're building at the intersection of AI and security, carving out an emerging market where the rules haven't been written yet, and the people who join now will write them.

We believe today's talent is tomorrow's success, and we're committed to creating an environment where you can do the best work of your life.

  • Recognized momentum - We made the Rising in Cyber 2026 list, a signal that the market is taking notice

  • Rare market opportunity - Join early in a category-defining company at the convergence of AI and security, where your work directly shapes how enterprises tackle one of the biggest unsolved problems in tech

  • Competitive pay and meaningful equity - A real stake in Harmonic's success, not a token gesture

  • Comprehensive benefits - 401K, pension plan, generous PTO, and flexible hybrid work

  • A small, high-trust team that values transparency, creativity, and continuous learning - no politics, no bureaucracy

  • Thoughtful leadership - that cares deeply about your growth, not just your output

  • Annual global off-sites - past trips include Lisbon, Portugal and Nashville, TN

  • Real ownership - you'll shape the product, the culture, and the direction of the company from day one

Harmonic's Core Values

🌱 Flourish in the Unknown

We embrace new, unfamiliar situations that require initiative and rapid decision-making. We orient ourselves quickly and deliver results with minimal guidance.

🔥 Never Full

We raise our hands, take on challenges, and assist others whenever possible. We hunger for opportunities to learn and do more.

🤝 Perfect Harmony

We support one another to create cohesion and unity. We collaborate openly, share feedback honestly, and help everyone produce their best work

Compensation: £98K – £110K • Offers Equity • Offers Bonus

raw.description:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Reporting to the VP, Legal Engineering & Regulatory Investigations, you will lead Harvey's Legal Engineering teams across EMEA.

You will directly manage Legal Engineering Managers and oversee the teams focused on supporting Harvey's pre-sales customer engagements. This is a second-line leadership role focused on organizational leadership, operational excellence, and cross-functional execution. This role will take full responsibility for establishing and defining the regional strategy for Harvey's Legal Engineering function as we scale.

Success in this role requires exceptional people leadership, strong business judgment, and the ability to build systems and processes that enable teams to operate effectively at scale. You will partner closely with leaders across Product, Engineering, Sales, Customer Success, and Operations to deliver exceptional outcomes for customers while helping shape the future of Legal Engineering at Harvey.

What You'll Do

  • Lead, develop, and scale a team of Legal Engineering Managers and their organizations serving Harvey's in-house customers.

  • Build the systems, processes, and operating mechanisms that enable Legal Engineering to deliver exceptional customer outcomes at scale.

  • Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Sales, Customer Success, and Operations to align priorities and drive execution across the business.

  • Act as a trusted advisor to law firm and legal department leaders and an influential partner to senior stakeholders across Harvey.

  • Drive organizational performance through effective planning, resource management, talent development, and operational excellence.

  • Help define the future of Legal Engineering.

What You Have

  • Qualified lawyer with 12+ years of post-qualification experience (PQE).

  • Experience practicing law at a top-tier law firm and/or in-house at a leading company, with significant client-facing experience.

  • Experience leading managers and manager-led organizations, not solely individual contributors.

  • Demonstrated success building and scaling high-performing teams in complex, fast-paced environments.

  • Experience owning organizational systems, processes, and operating models.

  • Proven ability to build strong cross-functional partnerships and drive results across multiple stakeholders.

  • Strong track record of managing upward and influencing senior leaders.

  • Experience representing an organization externally and building trusted relationships with executive-level stakeholders.

  • Deep understanding of law firms and enterprise legal teams, including corporate, litigation, investigations, regulatory, compliance, and legal operations functions, as well as the evolving legal technology landscape.

  • Exceptional communication, leadership, and organizational skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience leading teams outside of a traditional law firm hierarchy.

  • Experience in legal technology, professional services, consulting, legal innovation, legal operations, or other customer-facing organizations.

  • Experience operating in a high-growth technology company.

  • Experience leading globally distributed teams.

  • Demonstrated ability to create structure and drive execution in rapidly evolving environments.

  • Experience working across multiple legal practice areas, including corporate, litigation, investigations, regulatory, compliance, and legal operations.

raw.description:
Ironclad is the leading AI contracting platform that transforms agreements into assets. Contracts move faster, insights surface instantly, and agents push work forward, all with you in control. Whether you’re buying or selling, Ironclad unifies the entire process on one intelligent platform, providing leaders with the visibility they need to stay one step ahead. That’s why the world’s most transformative organizations, from Rivian to the World Health Organization and the Associated Press, trust Ironclad to accelerate their business.


We’re consistently recognized as a leader in the industry: a Leader in the Forrester Wave and Gartner Magic Quadrant for Contract Lifecycle Management, a Fortune Great Place to Work, and one of Fast Company’s Most Innovative Workplaces. Ironclad has also been named to Forbes’ AI 50 and Business Insider’s list of Companies to Bet Your Career On. We’re backed by leading investors including Accel, Y Combinator, Sequoia, BOND, and Franklin Templeton. For more information, visit www.ironcladapp.com or follow us on LinkedIn.

This is a hybrid role based out of our London office. Office attendance is required at least twice a week on Tuesdays and Thursdays out of our Moorgate office for collaboration and connection. There may be additional in-office days for team or company events.

Candidates must have the unrestricted right to work in the United Kingdom.

The Ironclad Adoption Strategist (AS) is a strategic role designed to accelerate customer adoption, increase user engagement, and maximise the business value of an organisation's Ironclad investment. The Adoption Strategist is Ironclad's primary customer-facing owner for enterprise and strategic accounts, responsible for leading customers from the first pre-sales service engagement through foundational adoption.

Working cross-functionally with Customer Value, Product, Sales, and Engineering teams, the adoption strategist develops adoption frameworks, accelerates user engagement, and designs implementation and adoption paths that are designed from the start to activate AI-powered workflows and deliver measurable outcomes that support long-term customer success.

The ideal candidate possesses a strong consulting mindset, exceptional communication skills, experience leading enterprise transformation initiatives, and deep knowledge of SaaS platforms, AI technologies, organisational change, and customer adoption methodologies.


What you'll be doing:

  • Partner with executive stakeholders to define business objectives, adoption strategies, and success metrics.

  • Develop and execute adoption roadmaps that accelerate user engagement and business value realisation for Ironclad’s enterprise and strategic customers.

  • Translate Ironclad's AI capabilities and evolving product motion into language and a delivery plan that resonates with executive stakeholders.

  • Partner closely with Contract AI Services to ensure that implementation and AI configuration work is designed to support the customer's long-term adoption path.

  • Own project execution end-to-end: manage timelines, track deliverables, identify and escalate risks, and maintain stakeholder alignment across internal and customer teams

  • Manage escalations with confidence — reset expectations, realign stakeholders, and resolve scope conflicts without waiting for leadership to intervene

  • Contribute to the improvement of delivery methodology, scoping playbooks, and adoption frameworks that scale the function's effectiveness over time

  • Monitor adoption metrics, customer health, and business outcomes; recommend continuous improvements based on data and customer feedback.

  • Collaborate across Customer Success, Professional Services, Product Management, Sales, Marketing, and Engineering to ensure a seamless customer experience and identify opportunities for growth and expansion.

  • Stay current on emerging AI technologies, SaaS capabilities, and industry best practices to continuously enhance customer value.


What we're looking for:

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Systems, Computer Science, Organisational Development, or a related technical field.

  • 5+ years of experience in Customer Success, Professional Services, Technology Consulting, Digital Transformation, Change Management, or Enterprise SaaS adoption.

  • Experience leading enterprise technology adoption or digital transformation initiatives.

  • Strong understanding of SaaS platforms, AI technologies, organisational change management, and customer success methodologies.

  • Demonstrated ability to influence executive stakeholders, facilitate cross-functional collaboration, and communicate complex concepts to both technical and business audiences.

  • Experience using adoption metrics and analytics to measure customer success and business outcomes.

  • Experience working with large enterprise customers and executive leadership teams.

UK Employee Benefits at Ironclad:

  • Private Medical & Dental insurance, covered at 100% for you and dependents

  • Life assurance and Income Protection

  • Generous leave policies, including parental leave, medical leave, and compassionate leave

  • Family-forming support through Maven for you and your partner

  • Monthly stipends for wellbeing, hybrid work, and (if applicable) phone use

  • Standard pension contribution scheme

  • Regular team events to connect, recharge, and have fun

  • And most importantly, the opportunity to help build the company you want to work at


US Full-Time Employee Benefits at Ironclad:

  • 100% health coverage for employees (medical, dental, and vision), and 75% coverage for dependents with buy-up plan options available

  • Market-leading leave policies, including gender-neutral parental leave and compassionate leave

  • Family forming support through Maven for you and your partner

  • Paid time off - take the time you need, when you need it

  • Monthly stipends for wellbeing, hybrid work, and (if applicable) cell phone use

  • Mental health support through Modern Health, including therapy, coaching, and digital tools

  • Pre-tax commuter benefits (US Employees)

  • 401(k) plan with Fidelity with employer match (US Employees)

  • Regular team events to connect, recharge, and have fun

  • And most importantly: the opportunity to help build the company you want to work at

raw.title: Director of People Operations
raw.description:
About Us

Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar.

Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes.

2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $200M+ in ARR, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler.

We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law.

Joining Legora means three things.

  • We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.

  • We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.

  • We grow together: as a team and with our customers.

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.


The role
This role owns how it works to be an employee at Legora on the backend. You will operationalise every stage of the employee journey, making sure every moment is supported by clean systems, accurate data, and processes that scale. If an employee interacts with a Legora program or system, from their first day in the HRIS to a salary change three years in, your team is accountable for making it accurate, timely, and smooth.

You will lead a distributed People Operations team across Stockholm and New York, reporting to the VP, People Operations. As we enter new markets, you will also build and manage local specialisms to handle day-to-day employee and manager questions and run structured, lower-complexity casework, with a clean handoff to Employee Relations for anything that becomes formal, contested, or carries legal weight.



What you'll own

  • The full employee lifecycle, operationally. Every touchpoint from offer to exit, mapped, documented, and supported end to end.

  • HRIS and data integrity. Onboarding new hires into the HRIS, data entry, and data QA. You keep employee data accurate, complete, and audit-ready as the single source of truth.

  • Contracts and changes. Addendums, employee transfers, salary and reporting-line changes, and the workflows and documentation behind each one, working in close partnership with Payroll so every change flows through accurately and on time.

  • Benefits and leave administration. Run the day-to-day administration of benefits and leave across our markets. Total Rewards owns the policies, plan design, and philosophy; your team makes sure they are executed cleanly for every employee. Anything contested, discriminatory, or medically complex is escalated to Employee Relations.

  • Local HR Generalist build-out. As Legora enters new markets, hire, ramp, and manage the local HR Generalist / People Advisor-Ops layer: the in-market presence for day-to-day employee and manager questions, and for structured, lower-complexity casework such as absence management, recurring capability concerns, and restructuring conversations. These roles report into People Operations for management and delivery, with a dotted line to the regional Employee Relations Director for sign-off on jurisdictional readiness and casework quality.

  • Systems and tooling. Run the People tech stack (HiBob, Ashby, Ironclad), drive adoption, and take manual work out of the process.

  • Process and SOPs. Design scalable, well-documented processes for every program employees touch, and keep reducing friction and cycle time.

  • Compliance and controls. Partner with Legal and Finance to keep operations compliant across our markets, including working time, leave, and entity or EOR transitions, with a clean escalation path to Employee Relations for anything that becomes formal or carries legal weight.

  • Reporting. Own people data quality and the reporting backbone that powers People analytics for the business.



What you'll bring

  • 8+ years in People Operations or HR Operations, including leading a team and building out local, in-market HR capability as a company scales into new geographies, ideally in a high-growth or global company.

  • Deep HRIS expertise across complex, multidisciplinary system landscapes, with a strong interest in data quality, integrations, AI and tools.

  • A track record of building and scaling lifecycle processes and SOPs internationally, and of moving work from manual to automated.

  • Strong grasp of multi-jurisdiction employment compliance across EMEA, AMER, and APAC.

  • Comfort operating in a tiered People model, with clear judgment on what your team owns directly and what belongs with Employee Relations, Legal, or Total Rewards.

  • An operator's mindset: detail-obsessed, systems-thinking, and a high bar for accuracy.

  • Comfort partnering across Finance, Legal, and IT, and communicating clearly with employees and leaders alike.

  • Fluency in English, which is our working language.


Why this role
 People Operations is the infrastructure that lets the rest of the People team, and the business, move fast without breaking things. That now includes building the in-market HR Generalist presence that gives every employee fast, consistent support close to home, wherever they are, with a clean handoff to Employee Relations the moment something becomes formal. You will build that infrastructure for one of the most exciting companies in tech, and set the standard for what operational excellence looks like as we scale.

Legora is an Equal Opportunity Employer

At Legora, we believe great teams are built on diversity of thought and experience. We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer and committed to creating an inclusive, high-performance culture where everyone can do their best work. We welcome people of all backgrounds and don’t discriminate based on race, color, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar.

Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes.

2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $200M+ in ARR, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler.

We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law.

Joining Legora means three things.

  • We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.

  • We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.

  • We grow together: as a team and with our customers.

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.

About us
At Legora, we’re changing how lawyers work. Our AI-native platform helps legal teams research, review, draft, and collaborate. We build closely with our clients and ship quickly across a growing number of markets.

The role

We’re hiring a Product Operations Manager to join our team and be part of the machine that facilitates product release management for the whole company and our clients.

You’ll own the operating system around releases for a specific product area: what is shipping, when it is ready, who needs to act, and what happens after launch. You’ll also improve how customer feedback and product data reach Product teams, so decisions are based on useful evidence rather than scattered requests.

You’ll need to be exceptionally comfortable with ambiguity and bring a practical, problem-solving mindset. You’ll jump into unfamiliar challenges, learn fast, and turn unclear problems into concrete next steps without waiting for a perfect brief or a ready-made playbook.

This is a hands-on individual-contributor role reporting to the Head of Product Operations. You’ll work across Product, Engineering, Support, Product Marketing, Engagement, and customer-facing teams in the US and Europe.

What you’ll do

  • Run release planning and readiness for major launches. Keep scope, owners, dependencies, risks, documentation, communications, and rollout decisions clear.

  • Maintain the company-facing view of the product roadmap and releases, and make sure partner teams have accurate information as plans change.

  • Build and maintain a reliable product-feedback process. Turn requests, support issues, and customer observations into evidence Product teams can prioritise and act on.

  • Track product and release health after launch. Use adoption data, operational metrics, and qualitative feedback to flag problems and recommend next steps.

  • Maintain the product knowledge layer across Notion, documentation as code, and other internal sources of truth. Improve the workflows and automation that keep it current.

  • Use agentic tooling and lightweight code to remove operational friction. Build scripts, ship small fixes, and support analysis without waiting for a dedicated Engineering cycle.

Who you are

  • You have 4+ years of experience in product operations, program management, business operations, consulting, technical program management, or a related role.

  • You have run complex launches or programs across Product, Engineering, or go-to-market teams.

  • You bring structure to unclear problems, make ownership explicit, and keep work moving when priorities change.

  • You communicate clearly with technical and non-technical teams and can influence without formal authority.

  • You are conversant in how software ships: you can work in a codebase, understand pull requests, and use agents to ship small fixes or analysis. You do not need to be a software engineer, but you should be comfortable working in code either directly or via agents.

  • Experience with enterprise software, release management, support operations, or product analytics is helpful. Legal experience is not required.

What’s in it for you

  • Broad ownership of how Legora launches and operates its product.

  • Direct collaboration with Product, Engineering, and go-to-market leaders across regions.

  • The chance to build systems that will shape how the company works as it scales.

  • Competitive compensation, benefits, and participation in Legora’s option program.

Legora is an Equal Opportunity Employer

At Legora, we believe great teams are built on diversity of thought and experience. As a Senior Enterprise Account Manager, you'll work with a book of global enterprise accounts — household names operating across multiple markets — to deepen their investment in monday.com and expand it. These are organisations at the forefront of enterprise AI transformation, moving fast to rewire their workflows, integrate intelligent agents into how they operate, and get ahead of competitors who aren't moving as quickly. Your job is to be the strategic partner that helps them do exactly that.

This is a quota-carrying role that requires strong executive-level sales skills, relationship-building capabilities, and a passion for delivering exceptional customer experiences.

 

Please note this is a hybrid role with a 3 day per week in the office requirement.

 

About the role;

  • The Account Manager position is a growth focused quota-carrying position; you will own the full sales cycle from generating opportunities, building strategic relationships with key stakeholders to negotiation, contracting and eventual renewal.

  • Research, identify, and engage opportunities within a territory of Enterprise accounts with existing spend. Proactively prospect into your accounts (cold calls, emails, social selling, networking, etc.) to build a robust pipeline.

  • Use the value framework and MEDDPICC to enact robust deal progression processes in collaboration with management to advance and close opportunities with new, complex use cases.

  • Strategically build relationships within accounts to build qualified champions. Gaining access to C-Level and VP economic buyers to ensure monday.com becomes a strategic partner of our Enterprise customers, aligned to corporate level goals.

  • Possess a comprehensive understanding of monday.com’s solution and connect this knowledge directly to customer ROI at the enterprise level.

  • Work closely with the Customer Success team and other internal stakeholders to create the conditions for account growth. This means setting the strategic direction, aligning internal resources, and ensuring monday.com shows up as one coordinated partner to our most demanding customers.

  • Continuously build and refine in-depth knowledge of the target industry, including trends, challenges, key players, and opportunities, to effectively position our solutions and add value to C-Level client conversations.

Requirements:

  • Experience: 5+ years of sales experience in a closing role at a SaaS or technology-related field, with a focus on larger Enterprise accounts with a global footprint.

  • Proven Success: Demonstrated track record of meeting or exceeding sales quotas and driving revenue growth with large, complex organizations. Experience of the Nordics region is preferred.

  • Sales Skills: Strong ability to prospect, qualify, and close deals with large, complex businesses. Experience with a consultative, value-based sales approach at the executive level.

  • Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication and negotiation skills with the ability to articulate complex concepts in a clear and relatable manner to senior stakeholders.

  • Tech-Savvy: Comfortable with technology, with the ability to quickly learn and demonstrate the functionality of software products, particularly in the context of enterprise solutions.

  • Disruptive technology: Experience selling genuinely new, category-defining technology. Comfortable helping customers navigate the shift from legacy ways of working to something meaningfully better.

  • CRM Proficiency: Experience with CRM tools such as Salesforce or HubSpot for managing sales activities and pipeline.

  • Internal leadership: Proven ability to lead without direct authority, rallying Solutions Engineers, Customer Success, Legal, and Executive sponsors around a shared account strategy. You're the person internal teams look to for direction on the accounts you own.

  • Problem Solver: Strong analytical and problem-solving skills to identify complex business challenges and develop tailored, enterprise-level solutions.

  • Customer-Centric: Passion for delivering exceptional customer experiences and adding strategic value to key client relationships.

  • Self-Starter: A proactive attitude with the ability to work independently, take initiative, and manage time effectively.

raw.title: Senior Strategy Manager
raw.description:
Centre for Net Zero is a not-for-profit open research institute established in 2021 as an autonomous part of the Octopus Energy Group. Our mission is to understand the world's changing potential for demand flexibility and make our evidence open and useful, so the world can run on clean electricity sooner and at lower cost. 

We design, run and evaluate global field trials to establish rigorous real world evidence; leverage advanced data science and open source modelling; build open source data, tools, and communities; and work with policymakers, industry leaders, and grid operators to turn our evidence into real world action.

About the role:

As we scale our research and ambitions, we are looking for a senior strategy manager to join our London team. You will work across CNZ's leadership team to increase the reach and impact of our work, at times operating in a capacity similar to a chief of staff. 


What you'll do
Most of your time:
  • Develop and scale (including securing resources where necessary) CNZ's strategic assets to increase overall impact in alignment with CNZ's mission. Examples of our strategic assets include our visiting researchers programme and our Faraday AI model. 
  • Lead research, market insights, and intelligence by curating external thinking, partnering with leading third parties to challenge our perspective, and using inventive methods to shape our research programme.
  • Drive strategic and tactical projects from problem to delivery, and contribute to others. This is likely to include projects in support of fundraising, and may include unusual or complex field trials or modelling partnerships.
    • Some of your time:
  • Own and deliver strategic organisational development initiatives, including driving the adoption of AI across the business.
  • Work closely with the CEO and executive team to drive operational excellence, championing a high-performing culture of rapid execution and seamless information flow.

    • What you'll need
  • Around 5+ years experience in a strategy consulting setting, or working closely with C-level execs or founders in a venture-backed startup.
  • Demonstrable interest in the research ecosystem, in the UK and internationally.
  • Strong interest in energy, able to learn quickly and communicate complex topics across sectors.
  • A proven track record of working independently, driving multiple priorities at once, and seeing projects through to the finish line.
  • An entrepreneurial instinct, able to shape ambiguity into opportunity and to separate productive risk-taking from imprudent decision making.
  • Strong writing, analytical skills, and critical thinking; you could spot and explain an overconfident or incorrect AI contribution that others would miss. 
  • Able to work from CNZ's office near Oxford Circus, a minimum of three days per week to start.
    • A bonus if you have:
  • Experience of securing philanthropic, foundation or grant funding.
  • Recent experience of using AI-based technologies to make organisations, teams and products better.
  • Experience of open source technologies, tools, and communities.

    • Why else you'll love it here

    • Wondering what the salary for this role is? Once you're in the interview process with one of our recruiters, it's something we always cover as we genuinely want to match your experience with the correct salary. The reason why we don't advertise is because we honestly have a degree of flexibility and would never want salary to be a reason why someone doesn't apply to Octopus - what's more important to us is finding the right octofit!
    • Octopus Energy Group is a unique culture. An organisation where people learn, decide, and build quicker. Where people work with autonomy, alongside a wide range of amazing co-owners, on projects that break new ground. We want your hard work to be rewarded with perks you actually care about! We were named the UK's top company to work for in 2025, and we ranked in the top ten in the Sunday Times Best Places to Work 2026. Our Group CEO, Greg has recorded a podcast about our culture and how we empower our people. We’ve also been placed in the top 10 companies for senior leadership
    • Visit our UK perks hub - Octopus Employee Benefits
     
    If this sounds like you then we'd love to hear from you, tell us what you care about, why Octopus feels right and most importantly, bring us the real you! Applying for jobs can be a bit scary so have a nose through some of our tips first 🚀
     
    P.S. Our process usually takes up to 4 weeks, but we’ll always do our best to flex around what works for you. Along the way, you’ll chat with our recruitment team and your Recruiter will help you throughout different stages. Got any burning questions before then? Drop us a message at ----- and we’d love to help!
     
    Are you ready for a career with us? We want to ensure you have all the tools and environment you need to unleash your potential. Need any specific accommodations? Whether you require specific accommodations or have a unique preference, let us know, and we'll do what we can to customise your interview process for comfort and maximum magic!

Whoever you are, if you like one of our jobs, we encourage you to apply as you might just be the candidate we hire. raw.description:
Established in 2004, OLIVER is the world's first and only specialist in designing, building, and running bespoke in-house agencies and marketing ecosystems for brands. We partner with over 300 clients in 40+ countries and counting. Our unique model drives creativity and efficiency, allowing us to deliver tailored solutions that resonate deeply with audiences. 

As a part of The Brandtech Group, we're at the forefront of leveraging cutting-edge AI technology to revolutionise how we create and deliver work. Our AI solutions enhance efficiency, spark creativity, and drive insightful decision-making, empowering our teams to produce innovative and impactful results. 

Role: Senior Content Manager - FTC

Location: London, United Kingdom

About the role: 

As Senior Content Manager, you'll own client's content strategy across multiple platforms - including Brandbank, Amazon Vendor Central, and PIM — and lead the workflows that bring it to life. You'll act as the connective tissue between brand, marketing, and creative teams, bringing strategic rigour and hands-on execution in equal measure. From NPD launches to ongoing content maintenance, you'll set the standard for quality and consistency across every channel.

What you will be doing: 

  • Develop and implement content strategy that serves client's commercial objectives, including A/B testing plans for Amazon product pages
  • Lead end-to-end content management across all publishing platforms: case raising, set-up, upload, editing, amends, and ongoing maintenance
  • Serve as NPD project lead for content creation, development, and publishing on DCOMM, ensuring best-in-class product launches
  • Manage content execution projects from scoping and asset review through to proposal creation and creative team alignment
  • Ensure all published content is accurate, on-brand, and error-free across every channel and platform
  • Collaborate with product, brand, and marketing teams to align content with strategic requirements and brand guidelines
  • Partner with the copywriter and designers to produce content that is visually rich and copy-strong, within best-in-class guidelines
  • Use data and commercial insight to inform content decisions and drive continuous improvement
  • Monitor team workflows and content management processes, ensuring adherence to agreed standards and timelines
  • Build proactive working relationships across the wider business, keeping key stakeholders informed and aligned 

What you need to be great in this role: 

  • Proven experience in content management, spanning strategy development, platform publishing, and end-to-end project delivery
  • Hands-on proficiency with Brandbank, Amazon Vendor Central, and PIM platforms
  • Experience managing content projects — scoping, briefing, asset review, proposal creation, and creative team alignment
  • Solid understanding of SEO principles and their application to product content and digital channels
  • Strong editing and proofreading skills, with a high standard of accuracy and attention to detail
  • Track record of leading, mentoring, and inspiring small creative teams
  • Collaborative working style, with the ability to build effective relationships across brand, product, and marketing functions
  • Data-informed approach to decision-making, with an understanding of how commercial priorities shape content strategy
  • Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and maintain quality under shifting timelines
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Planner
  • Experience within the alcohol, beverage, or FMCG sector (desirable)
  • Advanced use of Gen AI tools to enhance content output, workflow efficiency, and publishing quality
  • Experience designing AI-assisted workflows for yourself and your team
  • Ability to guide others on effective, responsible AI tool usage within a content context
  • Agentic approach to complex, multi-step content challenges — from brief through to live publication
  • Strong understanding of AI capabilities and limitations, with rigorous human oversight applied to all published content

raw.title: Operations Associate - Graduate Internship - November start
raw.description:
Note: Partly is headquartered in Austin, TX with offices in London, UK, Christchurch, NZ and Auckland, NZ. Wherever you're based, we'll connect you with your nearest office for onboarding, and fly you to join the full team for our quarterly "Season Openers" (we cover travel and accommodation). If you're relocating to join us, we can also assist with relocation costs.


🚀 Our Story

Partly is building the infrastructure for anyone to repair anything. We believe everything built should be repairable, and we're building frontier AI to put repair knowledge to work, starting with the $2tn automotive market.

Our model, Interpreter, is the first AI purpose-built to understand repair. Trained on 1M+ car models and 1B+ parts, it reads a repair job the way an estimator does, resolves damage into the exact purchasable part, and shows its reasoning with a confidence score. On real production jobs, an estimator working with Interpreter reaches 98.8% parts-list accuracy, against 92.1% with today's tools. It powers PartlyRepair, used by collision shops, workshops and suppliers to take the admin off the job; PartlyLabs, the agentic infrastructure enterprises use to deploy Interpreter across their own workflows; and a developer API.

Founded by ex-Rocket Lab engineers, we've raised a $50m Series B led by DST Global (Anthropic, Airbnb, Meta, TikTok, Spotify), with Blackbird Ventures, WNDR, Activant Capital, Icehouse Ventures, Square Peg, Airtree and Ecliptic Venture Capital. Hear it from the team: Why Partly exists and AI at Partly.

🖍️ This role

As the first time was a huge success, we're launching version 2 of Partly's Repairer Ambassador Programme — a 3-month, full-time (with flexibility), paid internship for a small cohort of sharp, driven graduates who want real responsibility from day one. This is for people who want something more than a coffee run and a PowerPoint, and will lead to a full-time role for those who make a genuine impact.

Your job is simple: get newly onboarded repair shops actively using the Partly platform as quickly as possible. That means building relationships on the ground, understanding why certain shops aren't placing orders through us, and removing those barriers. You'll become the human face of Partly in repair shops across the UK — someone repairers genuinely trust and enjoy working with.

This is not a desk job. You'll spend your first 1–2 weeks in our London office receiving structured training before heading out to visit customers across your assigned region.

Key details:

  • Contract: 3 months, full-time with flexibility

  • Start: As soon as possible - November 2026

  • Location: UK-wide (field-based, with initial training in London)

💻 What will you do

  • Visit newly signed repair shops across your region and help them get up and running on the Partly platform.

  • Understand why shops aren't placing jobs through Partly and identify practical ways to remove those barriers.

  • Help repairers optimise and streamline their parts procurement workflows.

  • Track repairer activity, monitor adoption, and report insights back to the team on what's working and what isn't.

  • Build authentic, long-term relationships with shop owners and parts managers.

  • Feed customer insights back to the wider business so we can continually improve the product and onboarding experience.

🥷 What we're looking for

  • A recent graduate (university, HND, engineering course, or apprenticeship) with a genuine hunger to learn and get stuck in.

  • Strong common sense and the ability to read a room. This role is all about building trust with people who work with their hands for a living.

  • A full UK driving licence (having your own car is a strong advantage).

  • Comfortable spending most of the week on the road visiting customers.

  • Organised, self-directed, and confident working independently.

  • Comfortable around automotive professionals. This could come from a genuine interest in cars, working on your own vehicle, following motorsport, spending time in automotive environments, or simply having the curiosity and confidence to quickly learn the industry's language and "talk shop" with customers.

🪅 What You’ll Get

  • £102 per day

  • Travel and accommodation costs covered

  • Real responsibility and customer-facing experience from week one

  • A strong reference and genuine insight into how a fast-growing tech company operates

  • A realistic path to a full-time role at Partly at the end of the programme for the people who excel

raw.description:
Note: Partly is headquartered in Austin, TX with offices in London, UK, Christchurch, NZ and Auckland, NZ. Wherever you're based, we'll connect you with your nearest office for onboarding, and fly you to join the full team for our quarterly "Season Openers" (we cover travel and accommodation). If you're relocating to join us, we can also assist with relocation costs.


🚀 Our Story

Partly is building the infrastructure for anyone to repair anything. We believe everything built should be repairable, and we're building frontier AI to put repair knowledge to work, starting with the $2tn automotive market.

Our model, Interpreter, is the first AI purpose-built to understand repair. Trained on 1M+ car models and 1B+ parts, it reads a repair job the way an estimator does, resolves damage into the exact purchasable part, and shows its reasoning with a confidence score. On real production jobs, an estimator working with Interpreter reaches 98.8% parts-list accuracy, against 92.1% with today's tools. It powers PartlyRepair, used by collision shops, workshops and suppliers to take the admin off the job; PartlyLabs, the agentic infrastructure enterprises use to deploy Interpreter across their own workflows; and a developer API.

Founded by ex-Rocket Lab engineers, we've raised a $50m Series B led by DST Global (Anthropic, Airbnb, Meta, TikTok, Spotify), with Blackbird Ventures, WNDR, Activant Capital, Icehouse Ventures, Square Peg, Airtree and Ecliptic Venture Capital. Hear it from the team: Why Partly exists and AI at Partly.

🖍️ This role

This is a product-builder role, not a ticket-taking one. You own a product surface end to end: you talk to the customer, form the idea, build it, ship it, measure it, and decide what happens next. The same person who understands the repairer writes the code. There is no handoff for product quality to leak through.

You'll build at the center of a multi-trillion-dollar industry that still runs on phone calls, spreadsheets, and tribal knowledge. Replacement parts is one of the largest physical markets on earth and one of the least digitised, and there is no established playbook to copy. Partly is creating the category.

Our moat is Interpreter, a domain-specific AI model that understands parts, vehicles, and the messy real-world relationships between them in ways general-purpose models cannot. It is what lets software finally make sense of a physical, offline industry, and it is the engine underneath everything you build.

And what you build is changing shape. We are not bolting AI onto old screens. We are creating genuinely new agentic experiences for a broad spectrum of users, from estimators and parts managers to accountants and suppliers, where people express intent and supervise outcomes while agents handle the mechanical work. Designing how that trust is earned, surface by surface, while each one still delivers value today, is the heart of the role.

You'll work at an inflection point in how software itself gets built. AI-assisted development has collapsed the distance between an idea and a working version of it. The builders we want already work this way: they prototype in an afternoon, put it in front of real customers within days, and read the signal themselves. We want someone who works like that now, or is visibly building toward it.

💻 What will you do

  • Build, not just specify. Prototype new product iterations yourself using AI-assisted and LLM-assisted tooling, fast, disposable, real. Treat the prototype as the hypothesis and put it in front of real customers before writing the spec. Ship production code, instrument it, and watch how it actually gets used.

  • Stay close to customers. Spend time where the work happens. Understand what estimators, parts managers, and others actually do, where they lose time, and what better would feel like. This is a core weekly activity, not an occasional input.

  • Reconcile signal. Combine what you see with what the data says, and reconcile the two when they disagree. Turn that understanding straight into what you build next.

  • Own the outcome. Steer by your surface's metrics; adoption and value delivered are yours. Make the call on priority and explain the reasoning, especially when the answer is no. When something is broken, own it, diagnose it precisely, and fix it.

  • Make the trade-off. Weigh product impact against engineering effort in the same breath, and find the cheaper path to the same outcome.

  • Build the agentic experience. Move your surface from manual operation toward supervised delegation: capture intent, decide where the human stays in the loop, and earn trust step by step so users never lose the thread of a high-stakes job.

  • Hold the craft. The surface feels fast, clear, and considered. You push back when something does not feel right, even when it technically works.

  • Raise the bar. Pair with SW Engineers on the harder systems work behind your surface, and contribute beyond your boundary: shared components, product craft, and what excellent building looks like here as the team grows.

🥷 Your skills

Non-negotiables

  • You ship end to end: a track record of taking features from idea to production, code included, with clear accountability for whether they worked. Roughly 3+ years building and shipping software in production.

  • Genuine customer obsession: a real habit of spending time with users in their work context, with a track record of that depth driving what you build.

  • Product taste and craft: the bar is experiences that feel effortless to time-pressured, non-technical users across fragmented, high-stakes workflows. Functional is not the finish line.

  • A point of view on agentic product design: how an experience moves from manual operation to supervised delegation, and how automation earns user trust gradually rather than all at once.

  • You build rapid prototypes yourself, with AI-assisted tools as a first instinct for testing an idea.

  • Solid full-stack engineering with a frontend lean: production-quality code and sound fundamentals. Systems-specialist depth is not the point of the role.

  • Trade-off fluency: you weigh product impact against engineering effort and often find a cheaper route to the same result.

  • Strong analytical instinct: you define the metric, build the view, read it, and act, without waiting for a data team.

  • You operate well in ambiguity and autonomy, and shape the problem rather than waiting for a spec.

Strong signals we look for

  • Shipped AI-assisted or agent-driven features in production, particularly where the human stays in the loop.

  • Built for a multi-persona, operational, or workflow-heavy B2B product.

  • Founder background, or early employee at a startup that scaled materially.

  • You've killed or radically changed something you personally believed in, and can explain why.

Bonus

  • Domain knowledge in automotive, the parts aftermarket, repair, or insurance claims.

  • Marketplace or network experience, from the demand or supply side.

  • Rust, or genuine eagerness to learn it. It is part of our stack.

Please note: if you don't have all the skills or experience listed above but believe you could be outstanding in this role, please still consider applying. Many people count themselves out. We'd love the chance to learn more about you and why you're exceptional.

🪅Benefits

  • Competitive base salary + equity. We offer competitive salaries and generous equity options for all full-time employees, ensuring everyone shares in the financial upside when we win.

  • Annual global offsite in New Zealand. Travel with the rest of the UK and EU team as we gather and connect for 1-2 weeks at our product and engineering hub in Christchurch.

  • Parental leave: Primary caregivers receive 3 months of fully paid parental leave, plus a flexible return-to-work (four days on full pay for your first three months back).

  • Team lunches: Lunch provided daily (Monday to Friday) in the office

  • Flexible working hours: We have flexible working hours and default to working from the office.

  • Season openers & events: We host regular events, including quarterly "season openers" for our UK/EU team, monthly team catch-ups, and weekly happy hours.

  • Healthy body, healthy mind: Every team member gets a £750 annual wellness allowance on a Partly-branded card. Use on gym memberships, rock climbing, physio, massage, GP visits, prescriptions; anything that you or your family, need.

raw.title: Data Center Architect
raw.description:
Role Profile

Job Title: Data Centre Architect

Reports to: Head of Data Centre Development

Location: UK hybrid

Company Overview:

Radiant is redefining how AI infrastructure is built.

We design and operate AI-native cloud platforms engineered for sovereignty, performance, and scale. Our infrastructure powers GPU-native workloads, multi-tenant control planes, and high-performance AI systems designed for the most demanding environments.

We are not building a generic cloud. We are building purpose-built AI infrastructure — from powered land, to compute, to software.

As we scale, we’re building this organisation from the ground up. We’re looking for people who’d rather build the playbook than inherit one — who are comfortable doing the work themselves as well as directing others, and who can adapt as fast as our strategy does. This is a startup model: attitude and adaptability matter more to us than years of experience or the size of team you’ve previously managed.

This is a senior individual contributor role with authority to sign off technical schedules, working with cluster and network architects, NVIDIA and other OEM engineers, colocation provider engineering and sales teams, and the internal Procurement, Legal, Finance and Site Operations teams.

What You’ll Do

You will be the single technical authority between our GPU-as-a-service business and the colocation providers that host our NVIDIA clusters. You turn cluster architecture and OEM requirements into a precise, contractable statement of work (SOW) for the data centre white space, then hold the provider to it through design, installation and acceptance.

We are growing from tens of megawatts to hundreds, on rack-scale liquid-cooled platforms at 130 kW per rack and rising to 200 kW and beyond. Mistakes in power, cooling or fibre specification show up as stranded capacity, delayed cluster delivery and disputes, so the role carries real commercial weight.

Key Responsibilities

Technical negotiation with colocation providers

  • Lead technical due diligence on candidate sites: power availability and energisation dates, redundancy topology, liquid-cooling capability, floor loading, rack logistics, fibre and meet-me access.

  • Negotiate the technical schedules of the colocation agreement with commercial and legal: capacity and density commitments, power and cooling SLAs, temperature and flow envelopes, metering, expansion rights, change control and remedies.

  • Challenge provider claims with evidence: single-line diagrams, P&IDs, load-bank and commissioning records, reference customers.

Specification & SOW

  • Work with cluster architects and OEMs (NVIDIA first) to capture rack, power, cooling, network and layout requirements, and keep them current across product generations.

  • Write and own the technical SOW for white-space fitout: containment and cooling interfaces, power distribution to rack, structured cabling and pathways, rack and POD layout, security zoning, labelling and records.

  • Define clear scope boundaries and responsibilities between us, the colocation provider, OEMs and installation contractors, with no gaps and no overlaps.

  • Maintain a requirements baseline with traceability from OEM document, to SOW clause, to acceptance test.

Design, installation & acceptance

  • Review provider and contractor designs, shop drawings and method statements against the SOW; run design reviews and close findings.

  • Define acceptance: factory and site tests, liquid flush and cleanliness, power quality, thermal performance at full load, fibre loss, burn-in, and the evidence pack needed for each gate.

  • Attend key witness tests and sign off, or reject, completion of each phase before hardware is energised.

  • Manage technical change requests and variations, and advise on cost and schedule impact.

Knowledge & standards

  • Build reusable reference designs, SOW templates and a site-scoring framework so each new deployment starts from a proven baseline.

  • Track the roadmap: higher rack densities, 800 VDC distribution, new cooling classes and optics, and tell the business early what it means for sites already contracted.

Deliverables You Own:

  • Site technical assessment: Scored, evidence-based report per candidate site, comparable across providers, with risks and mitigations.

  • Technical schedules to the colocation agreement: Measurable commitments, tested in acceptance, with remedies agreed by legal.

  • Cluster white-space SOW: Complete enough that a contractor can price and build without asking us questions; traceable to OEM requirements.

  • Reference designs and layouts: Rack, row and POD layouts, power and cooling single-line and P&ID level interfaces, fibre pathways and densities.

  • Acceptance test plan and evidence pack: Pass and fail criteria set before work starts; signed results per gate.

raw.title: Global Capability Centre UK Lead
raw.description:
About Radiant

Radiant builds and operates AI-native cloud platforms for high-performance GPU workloads. Our infrastructure brings together data centres, compute, networking, storage and software to serve customers with demanding AI requirements.

As we grow internationally, we are establishing Global Capability Centres (GCCs) in several regions. These centres will provide specialist capability and operational support to teams across Radiant. We need a clear model for how each centre is launched, managed and connected to the wider business.

About the role

The Global Capability Centre UK Lead will help design, launch and scale Radiant’s GCCs. You will work closely with local GCC leaders and UK teams across People, Legal, Finance, IT, Security and Operations.

Your job is to make sure each centre has a defined purpose, an effective team structure, practical ways of working and the support it needs to deliver. You will also act as a point of contact and advocate for GCC leaders in the UK, helping resolve issues that span multiple teams or locations.

This is a hands-on, cross-functional role. You will help shape the overall model while also dealing with the details that determine whether a new centre works well from day one.

What you’ll do:

Plan and launch GCCs

  • Help assess potential locations based on talent availability, cost, time zones, regulation and operational needs.

  • Define the remit of each centre with local and UK leaders. Clarify which work belongs in the GCC, which stays with existing teams and how responsibilities may change as the centre grows.

  • Support launch plans, including the order in which centres and functions are established, key decisions, dependencies and transition milestones.

  • Coordinate with Legal, Finance, People and Security on entity setup, employment arrangements, data residency and other local requirements.

Build teams and operating models

  • Work with GCC leaders to design team structures, reporting lines and management layers that suit each stage of growth.

  • Partner with Talent Acquisition on headcount plans, hiring priorities and the skills needed to deliver each centre’s remit.

  • Align roles and career paths with Radiant’s global framework. Help local leaders plan for retention, succession and leadership development.

  • Define ownership, handoffs and escalation routes between GCCs and UK functions so work moves smoothly across teams and time zones.

  • Establish consistent core processes while adapting them where local law, customer requirements or operating conditions call for it.

  • Make sure onboarding, equipment, systems access and operational support are ready as teams join. Track time to productivity and address recurring blockers.

Connect GCCs with the wider business

  • Serve as the UK point of contact for GCC leaders, holding regular check-ins to surface risks, resolve issues and share good practice.

  • Bring together the right support from People, Legal, Finance, IT, Security and Operations when a centre needs a decision or intervention.

  • Help build effective communication and one Radiant culture across locations, while recognising the needs of local teams.

Manage governance and performance

  • Establish steering meetings and operating reviews with clear decisions, owners and follow-up actions.

  • Maintain a risk register for each centre covering people, delivery, security, compliance and commercial risks. Work with specialist teams on data protection, information security, export controls and local regulatory obligations.

  • Define useful measures for cost, hiring, productivity, retention, service quality and delivery. Report progress against each centre’s business case to Radiant leadership.

  • Identify when a GCC is ready to take on more complex or higher-value work, and help plan that expansion.

What you’ll bring

  • Experience building, launching, scaling or operating GCCs, shared service centres, delivery centres or similar international teams.

  • Strong experience in operating model design, organisation design and workforce planning. You can turn a broad plan into clear roles, processes and decisions.

  • Experience coordinating complex work across countries, cultures and functions, with the judgement to balance global consistency and local needs.

  • Commercial awareness and experience tracking budgets, business cases or operational performance.

  • Practical experience establishing governance, managing risks and working with specialist teams on international employment, security or compliance matters.

  • The ability to influence senior stakeholders and local leaders without relying on direct authority.

  • Clear written and verbal communication, comfort working in an evolving organisation and willingness to travel internationally.

Nice to have

Experience in technology, cloud or infrastructure businesses; setting up international entities or operating models; managing data residency or export control requirements; or supporting post-acquisition integration.

raw.title: Infrastructure Tooling & Observability Engineer (UK)
raw.description:
About Us

We’re a fast-growing GPU-as-a-Service provider, delivering scalable, high-performance compute infrastructure purpose-built for AI and HPC workloads. Operating across global data centres, we run mission-critical environments where uptime, throughput, and ultra-low latency are non-negotiable.

Role Overview

We are seeking an Infrastructure Tooling & Observability Engineer to act as a key engineering force within our global Infrastructure Operations organisation. Working closely with our SRE teams, you will translate high-level reliability objectives into scalable, production-ready systems that directly improve the resilience, efficiency, and performance of our global infrastructure.

This role goes beyond traditional monitoring. You will help design and build the internal control plane that enables operations at scale across a rapidly growing GPU fleet. Your work will focus on transforming complex, high-volume telemetry—spanning logs, metrics, and events across HPC, networking, and platform layers—into actionable insight that drives operational excellence and proactive reliability.

A core part of your responsibility will be developing intelligent observability and automation systems, including advanced alerting strategies, anomaly detection, and AI-driven tooling that reduces L1/L2 escalations and removes operational toil. You will also contribute to Continual Service Improvement (CSI) initiatives by building frameworks for reliability measurement, automated remediation, and system health evaluation.

In addition, you will play a central role in turning SRE reliability initiatives into scalable engineering solutions. This includes designing and delivering capabilities such as inventory management systems, performance testing frameworks, and automated performance result collection. You will also help eliminate manual workflows involved in onboarding new regions, facilities, and clusters, embedding automation and standardisation into every stage of infrastructure deployment.

As the organisation scales, you will act as a critical interface between operations and engineering teams. You will evaluate and mature internally built tooling—from capacity planning systems to autonomous remediation pipelines—and help integrate these capabilities into core infrastructure platforms to ensure consistent, high-performance, and highly reliable global operations.

What’s In it for you?

Join a team building the internal platforms that enable large-scale infrastructure to operate reliably, efficiently, and at speed. As an Infrastructure Tooling & Observability Engineer, you will design and develop the systems that power visibility, automation, and operational intelligence across complex distributed environments.

This role goes beyond traditional monitoring. You will build the internal control plane that transforms high-volume telemetry—logs, metrics, and events—into actionable insight for engineering and operations teams. Your work will improve observability across infrastructure systems, strengthen signal quality, and help teams understand and respond to system behaviour in real time.

Working closely with SRE and infrastructure engineering teams, you will translate reliability goals into scalable, production-grade tooling. This includes frameworks for observability, alerting, anomaly detection, capacity planning, and service health tracking.

A key focus of the role is automation. You will help eliminate manual processes across infrastructure operations, including environment provisioning, cluster onboarding, inventory management, and recurring operational workflows. You will also contribute to performance engineering initiatives, building tooling for testing, benchmarking, and automated results collection at scale.

You will play a central role in turning SRE reliability initiatives into reusable engineering solutions, including automated remediation systems and tooling that reduces operational toil while improving system resilience.

You can also expect:

Exposure to large-scale distributed infrastructure systems
Opportunities to shape foundational internal platforms
A collaborative, engineering-led culture with strong ownership
High-impact work spanning observability, automation, and reliability
Close partnership with SRE and infrastructure engineering teams
A fast-moving environment where tooling directly improves operational performance

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and evolve internal tooling and observability platforms that support large-scale infrastructure operations across distributed environments.

  • Develop systems that turn high-volume telemetry (logs, metrics, events) into actionable insight, improving visibility, alerting quality, and operational decision-making.

  • Translate SRE reliability requirements into scalable, production-ready software solutions, including automation for incident detection, prevention, and remediation.

  • Drive automation across infrastructure operations, reducing manual effort in areas such as environment provisioning, cluster onboarding, inventory management, and lifecycle workflows.

  • Build tooling for capacity management, performance testing, benchmarking, and automated collection and analysis of results.

  • Contribute to Continual Service Improvement (CSI) initiatives by identifying operational inefficiencies and delivering durable engineering solutions.

  • Work closely with SRE and infrastructure engineering teams to embed observability and reliability into core platform workflows.

  • Interface with Platform Engineering teams to ensure tooling aligns with broader orchestration and infrastructure strategy.

  • Integrate and extend existing systems written in Ruby/Rails and Go, contributing to a consistent and maintainable engineering ecosystem.

  • Develop and maintain automation workflows using Ansible and AWX.

  • Support CI/CD-driven operational tooling, including GitHub Actions and self-hosted runners.

Essential Skills & Experience

  • Degree in Computer Science/Software Engineering, or equivalent experience

  • 6–8 years of experience in infrastructure engineering, DevOps, SRE, and/or software engineering roles, with a strong focus on operational systems.

  • Proven experience in at least one recent DevOps or software engineering role, building or maintaining production infrastructure tooling or platform systems.

  • Experience working in large-scale or distributed infrastructure environments (hyperscale, enterprise, or similarly complex systems).

  • Strong programming ability in at least one of: Ruby (Rails), Go, or similar systems languages, with willingness and ability to work across multiple languages and codebases.

  • Hands-on experience with infrastructure automation tools such as Ansible and orchestration platforms such as AWX.

  • Strong experience with observability systems, including the Grafana stack (Prometheus, Loki, Mimir, and Grafana Alloy).

  • Familiarity with low-level telemetry and infrastructure protocols such as SNMP and syslog.

  • Experience working with Kubernetes or similar orchestration platforms in production environments.

  • Understanding of API design and integration patterns, particularly REST-based services and service-to-service communication.

  • Experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines, including GitHub Actions and self-hosted runners.

  • Strong understanding of operational reliability concepts, including monitoring, alerting, capacity planning, and incident response.

  • Comfortable working closely with SRE, Platform Engineering, and infrastructure teams to translate operational needs into maintainable software systems.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Kubernetes Certified Administrator

  • Cloud-native observability training courses, attendance at industry conferences in this field

  • CompTIA+ Security Qualifications

  • LPI/LPIC certification

Commercial Product Manager
raw.description:
About us

At STRATOS Technologies, we are transforming how companies make data-driven decisions. Our software integrates complex datasets into a unified solution, enabling businesses to strengthen their long-term strategies through clear and actionable insights.

Our founders, former business and tech executives who led a $1B division at a Fortune 500 industrial company, originally built a digital twin of their enterprise to drive synchronized planning and execution. Seeing the market’s lack of such a system, they launched STRATOS in 2022 with a bold mission: to unifiy all internal and external data into a single platform.

Today, STRATOS is a category-defining, rapidly growing startup funded extensively by high-profile investors (e.g., Accel) and trusted by nearly a dozen global industrial leaders and Fortune 500 customers. Our software integrates complex datasets into a unified solution, combining deep data integration, best-in-class workflows, and cutting-edge generative AI.

From commercial AI agents to embedded intelligence that supercharges lean teams, STRATOS enables businesses to achieve 10x productivity and strengthen long-term strategies through actionable insights. We are now expanding our team to accelerate our growth even further and help our customers outperform their competition

The role. You own a piece of the relationship with one of our customers: their data, their questions, and whether the product answers them. You will do the analysis, present it to their commercial leadership, and take what you learn back to our engineers as something we should build. The difference from where you are now is that you stay with it. You see whether the recommendation worked, and when it doesn't, you're the one who fixes it.

The roles you'll play

  • Owner of a workstream — take a defined part of the deployment end to end: the market model, the target list or the scoring logic, from first data through to something the customer's teams use every week.

  • Advisor to the customer's commercial team — run working sessions with sales and commercial leadership, present your own analysis, and handle the challenge yourself. You are in the room, not behind it.

  • Co-owner of the account — you share the relationship with a senior CPM and take on more of it as the year goes on, up to running a customer of your own.

  • Voice of the customer in our roadmap — turn what you see in the field into what we build, and stay with it through the roadmap until it ships.

  • Builder of how we work — sharpen the standards, templates and tooling that make the next deployment better than the last.

Who this is for. Most people who do well here have one to three years behind them in strategy consulting, corporate strategy, or an analytical commercial role.

  • You have run a workstream yourself: not just the analysis, but the stakeholder who didn't want to give you the data and the deadline that moved.

  • You are quick in data and you check your own numbers. Excel and PowerPoint are assumed; any SQL or Python is a bonus, not a requirement, and we'll teach you what you need.

  • You can present to people twenty years your senior without either deferring to them or lecturing them.

  • You are curious about how industrial businesses actually work — how a building-materials group reaches its customers, why a distributor behaves the way it does.

  • You want more responsibility than your peers get, and you understand that comes with being the one who is wrong in public sometimes.

This probably isn't for you if you want to specialise early, or if you'd rather be handed a defined analysis than decide what the right question is.

What we offer

  • Equity through our stock option programme, so you share in the long-term success and growth of the company

  • A highly competitive salary

  • Direct access to Fortune 500 executives from your first months, at a level most people wait a decade for

  • Work alongside former MBB consultants and Fortune 500 executives who will teach you directly — our team is small enough that this happens in person, not through a training curriculum

  • Private healthcare

  • Pension scheme

  • 25 days of annual leave, plus bank holidays

  • Work from abroad — up to four weeks a year, and up to two weeks at a time

  • Hybrid office policy, with visa sponsorship available

  • A company committed to social and environmental responsibility — we pledge to be a net-zero CO₂ company and donate 1% of our revenue to social causes

Practicalities

  • London-based, 3 days a week in our Farringdon office

  • Travel to some customer sites around, mostly within Europe

  • German is genuinely useful here and several of our customers are German-speaking, but it is not a requirement

The process

  1. First round with our Talent Lead — 30 minutes

  1. Tehcncial case interview — 45 minutes

  1. Hiring manager interview with a senior executive - 30 minutes

  1. Second senior executive interview, which may include a case exercise - 30 minutes

  1. Final stage with our CEO - 45 minutes
